questions.question: Personnel Management is primarily concerned with—
options: acquisition and utilization of human beings for organizational objectives
questions.explanation: The 2026 paper defines Personnel Management as the arm of management dealing with the acquisition and utilization of human beings to accomplish organizational goals

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT identified in the 2025 paper as part of management activities under Personnel Management?
questions.explanation: Recruitment, manpower planning and employee training are identified management activities; road construction is not.

questions.question: According to the 2025 paper, Personnel Management in government is concerned with the effective and efficient—
options: utilization, motivation and protection of staff
taxation, budgeting and auditing of staff
questions.explanation: The three closely inter-related functions identified are utilization, motivation and protection of staff.

questions.question: Which activity falls primarily under personnel utilization?
questions.explanation: Personnel utilization includes promotion, appraisal, training and development.

questions.question: Which of the following is associated with personnel motivation?
questions.explanation: The paper places salaries, fringe benefits, job satisfaction, consultation and negotiation under personnel motivation.

questions.question: The 2025 paper cautions that the protection function of Personnel Management becomes meaningful only when—
options: utilization and motivation functions have been properly addressed
all staff have reached retirement age
questions.explanation: The paper expressly links personnel protection to proper utilization and motivation.

questions.question: Which of the following is associated with personnel deployment?
options: Designation of officers and assignment of responsibilities
questions.explanation: Deployment includes designation of officers, assignment of responsibilities and posting.

questions.question: Personnel Management also includes the maintenance of public organization, which refers primarily to—
options: keeping the organization running effectively on a day-to-day basis
questions.explanation: The paper describes maintenance as keeping the organization running effectively in its day-to-day operations.

questions.question: Which management functions were summarized by L. Qulick using the acronym POSDCOKB?
options: Planning, Organising, Staffing, Directing, Controlling, Coordinating, Reporting and Budgeting
Planning, Ordering, Staffing, Delegating, Controlling, Operating, Keeping and Banking
Procurement, Organising, Selection, Development, Coordination, Knowledge and Budgeting
Planning, Operations, Staffing, Discipline, Communication, Organization, Knowledge and Benefits
questions.explanation: The 2026 paper lists Planning, Organising, Staffing, Directing, Controlling, Coordinating, Reporting and Budgeting and associates them with POSDCOKB.

questions.question: A supervisor who manages people working under him is, according to the 2025 paper, performing—
options: no personnel function unless he works in the Directorate of Administration
questions.explanation: The paper emphasizes that managers at various levels perform personnel functions, even though certain officers are formally designated personnel officers.

questions.question: Who are specifically designated as Personnel Managers/Officers in the Civil Service according to the 2025 paper?
options: Administrative and executive officers in the Directorate of Administration
questions.explanation: The paper identifies administrative and executive officers in the Directorate of Administration as specifically designated Personnel Managers/Officers.

questions.question: Which statement BEST reflects the paper's treatment of the term “Personnel Manager”?
options: It applies exclusively to officers in the Directorate of Administration.
It can apply to anyone involved in day-to-day management of people and resources.
It applies only to Permanent Secretaries.
It applies only to Civil Service Commission members.
questions.explanation: The paper says all those involved in day-to-day management of people and resources perform personnel-management functions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a basic tool for personnel management?
questions.explanation: The listed tools include PSRs, circulars, schemes of service, annual appropriation laws and financial regulations.

questions.question: The Public Service Rules primarily help to—
options: streamline human/personality differences and problems that may reduce productivity
determine the price of government land
questions.explanation: The 2025 paper describes the PSRs as helping to streamline differences and problems among personnel and guide them in performing duties.

questions.question: Which tool provides information on posts, salaries, duties, entry into cadres and career advancement?
questions.explanation: The Scheme of Service provides information on posts, salaries, duties, entry methods and career advancement.

questions.question: A public servant claims not to know the duties attached to his position. Which source should he consult most directly?
questions.explanation: The paper specifically notes that responsibilities are clearly stated in the Scheme of Service.

questions.question: Government circulars may be issued to—
options: clarify an existing rule, fill an observed gap or introduce a new rule
determine individual salaries without reference to rules
questions.explanation: Those three purposes are expressly identified in the paper.

questions.question: Which is an example of a circular source identified in the 2025 paper?
questions.explanation: The paper lists Civil Service Commission, Head of Service, Establishment and Ministry of Finance/Accountant-General circulars.

questions.question: Financial Regulations guide public officers primarily in—
questions.explanation: The paper identifies receipt, custody and accounting of revenue and procurement, custody and utilization of stores/assets.

questions.question: Which of the following is a stated function of Personnel Management in government?
questions.explanation: The paper expressly includes policies, procedures, procurement, deployment and maintenance.

questions.question: Under the 2026 paper, the State Civil Service Commission has constitutional responsibility to—
options: appoint persons to offices in the State Civil Service and exercise disciplinary control
manage every private employee in the State
questions.explanation: The paper cites Section 197 and identifies appointment and disciplinary control over State Civil Service officers.

questions.question: The Civil Service Commission's constitutional personnel responsibility relates specifically to the—
questions.explanation: The 2026 paper expressly distinguishes State Civil Service officers appointed by the Commission from broader Public Service employees appointed by various bodies.

questions.question: Which body is described as an independent body in performing its constitutional appointment, promotion and disciplinary functions?
questions.explanation: The 2025 paper describes the CSC as constitutionally responsible for appointment, promotion and discipline and says it is independent in performing these functions.

questions.question: CSC Circular No. 1/2000 provided for delegation of appointment, promotion and discipline of officers on—
questions.explanation: The 2026 paper states that the CSC delegated powers concerning officers on salary grades 01–06 to MDAs.

questions.question: The Junior Staff Committee primarily handles matters concerning officers on—
questions.explanation: The JSC handles matters concerning officers on GL 01–06.

questions.question: The Senior Staff Management Committee handles matters concerning officers on—
questions.explanation: The SSMC handles officers on salary grades 07–17.

questions.question: Recommendations of the JSC are approved by the—
options: Head of Service personally in every case
questions.explanation: The 2025 paper states that the Permanent Secretary is the approving authority for JSC decisions and recommendations.

questions.question: The SSMC makes recommendations to the—
questions.explanation: The SSMC handles GL 07–17 matters and makes recommendations to the CSC for final determination.

questions.question: An officer dissatisfied with a JSC decision wishes to petition the Governor directly. According to the seminar, the officer should instead—
options: bypass all committees because the Governor is final authority
follow the relevant personnel-management committee route
write directly to the Head of Service
questions.explanation: The paper states that officers should not write directly on personnel matters to the Head of Service or Governor without passing through relevant management committees.

questions.question: Which body is responsible for record keeping, documentation, pension matters and training?
questions.explanation: These responsibilities are assigned to the Department of Establishments

questions.question: Which Department acts as a clearing house for personnel-management matters at State level?
questions.explanation: The Department of Establishments serves as the clearing house through regulations on personnel management matters at State level.

questions.question: Training is described in the seminar as a requirement for—
questions.explanation: The Department of Establishments' training function is described as a requirement for progression.

questions.question: Applications for public-service training are initially received by the—
questions.explanation: Applications are received by the respective Departmental Selection Board of each Ministry or pooling department.

questions.question: The Office of the Head of Civil Service is described as coordinating—
options: all administrative functions of the State Public Service
questions.explanation: That coordinating responsibility is expressly identified in the 2025 paper.

questions.question: Which of the following is listed among personnel-related commissions?
questions.explanation: The 2026 paper identifies the Civil Service, Local Government Service and Judiciary Service Commissions among the constitutional personnel organs.

questions.question: Recruitment is defined in the 2025 paper as the process of—
options: sourcing and selecting a suitable candidate for an available vacancy
questions.explanation: That is the paper's definition of recruitment.

questions.question: Recruitment of officers on GL 07 and above is done by the—
questions.explanation: The 2025 paper assigns recruitment of GL 07 and above to the CSC.

questions.question: Recruitment of officers on GL 01–06 has been delegated to—
questions.explanation: The CSC delegated recruitment of GL 01–06 to respective Ministries or Departments.

questions.question: When filling an existing vacancy, the scheme that should be strictly adhered to is the—
questions.explanation: The paper specifically states that the Scheme of Service should be strictly adhered to when appointing persons to fill existing vacancies.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four appointment types identified under PSR 020202?
options: Appointment on probation in a pensionable post
Appointment on permanent basis without probation
questions.explanation: The four types are probationary pensionable, non-pensionable/contract, temporary and acting appointments.

questions.question: A contract appointment described in the seminar may vary between—
questions.explanation: Non-pensionable contract appointments are stated as varying between 12, 18 or 24 months.

questions.question: An appointment made on a daily or monthly basis falls under—
questions.explanation: Temporary appointment may be on a daily or monthly basis.

questions.question: An officer appointed on probation in a pensionable post should ensure confirmation after—
questions.explanation: The seminar states that confirmation should occur on completion of two years of probation.

questions.question: Failure to secure confirmation after the probationary period may result in—
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically warns that failure to confirm the appointment may result in future stagnation.

questions.question: Which age range is stated for permanent/pensionable appointment?
questions.explanation: The 2026 paper states that a candidate should not be below 18 or above 50 years.

questions.question: Which qualification is specifically required for permanent/pensionable appointment?
options: Minimum qualification specified in the Scheme of Service
Any qualification chosen by the applicant
questions.explanation: The candidate must possess the required minimum qualification specified in the Scheme of Service.

questions.question: Fitness for permanent/pensionable appointment is to be certified by a—
questions.explanation: The paper requires certification of physical fitness and mental soundness by a Government Medical Officer.

questions.question: Which document relating to past conduct is listed among appointment requirements?
questions.explanation: A testimonial of conduct for past records is expressly listed.

questions.question: A candidate for permanent/pensionable appointment must possess a certificate of origin from—
options: his or her Local Government Area
questions.explanation: The requirement is a certificate of origin from the candidate's LGA.

questions.question: Which NYSC document is accepted for the appointment requirement described in the paper?
questions.explanation: The paper specifies NYSC Discharge Certificate or Exemption Certificate.

questions.question: Which candidate would conflict with the stated appointment requirements?
options: A qualified candidate aged 35 with an NYSC discharge certificate
A candidate who is an ex-convict
A candidate certified physically and mentally fit
A candidate with a required Scheme-of-Service qualification
questions.explanation: The paper states that the candidate must not be an ex-convict or formerly dismissed from service.

questions.question: A candidate has already retired from a previous service. According to the listed requirements, this candidate—
options: does not satisfy the stated condition
is automatically appointed in an acting capacity
questions.explanation: The paper lists “was not already retired from previous service” among the requirements.

questions.question: The requirement concerning financial embarrassment relates to ensuring that the candidate—
options: has no primary obligation of financial embarrassment
receives no salary from another source
questions.explanation: This is the wording used in the source.

questions.question: According to the 2026 paper, recruitment and appointment approvals under the current practice are approved by the—
questions.explanation: The paper says the current practice is that all recruitments and appointments are approved by the Governor, with the stated purpose of budgetary control, uniformity and standardization.

questions.question: The stated purpose of approval of recruitments and appointments by the Governor is to ensure—
options: elimination of the Scheme of Service
questions.explanation: Those three purposes are expressly stated.

questions.question: The seminar distinguishes transfer-of-service and secondment from—
options: routine posting or deployment in MDAs
questions.explanation: The paper explicitly says transfer-of-service and secondment are quite different from routine posting/deployment.

questions.question: Which is a type of transfer-of-service identified in the paper?
questions.explanation: Inter-Ministerial/Inter-Departmental transfer is expressly listed.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a type of transfer-of-service?
questions.explanation: The paper lists Inter-Ministerial/Inter-Departmental, Inter-Service, Inter-Cadre and Inter-State transfers.

questions.question: Secondment refers to the temporary release of an officer to—
questions.explanation: The paper defines secondment as temporary release to another Government or approved body.

questions.question: The period of secondment described in the paper is—
questions.explanation: The paper specifies a period of two years, depending on the type of secondment.

questions.question: Secondment may occur—
options: on the officer's request or in public interest/policy
questions.explanation: Both the officer's request and public interest/policy are identified.

questions.question: Which scenario BEST represents secondment?
options: An officer is temporarily released to another approved government body for a specified period.
An officer is assigned another desk in the same office.
questions.explanation: This matches the source definition of secondment.

questions.question: Promotion is described in the 2025 paper primarily as—
options: a reward for hard work and encouragement toward greater performance
questions.explanation: The paper describes promotion as a reward for hard work and a means of encouraging performance and productivity.

questions.question: Promotion is essentially a function of the—
questions.explanation: The source identifies promotion as essentially a CSC function, subject to delegated powers.

questions.question: The CSC has delegated promotion of officers on GL 01–06 to—
options: Permanent Secretaries and Heads of Department
questions.explanation: The 2025 paper states that Permanent Secretaries and Heads of Department promote officers on GL 01–06 under delegated authority.

questions.question: The CSC promotes officers on—
questions.explanation: The CSC retains promotion of officers on GL 07 and above.

questions.question: Which scenario is correctly matched?
options: GL 09 promotion — Permanent Secretary under the stated delegation
GL 04 promotion — delegated to appropriate authority
questions.explanation: The source places GL 01–06 promotion under delegated authority, while CSC promotes GL 07 and above.

questions.question: A promotion system intended to encourage greater productivity demonstrates promotion's role as—
questions.explanation: The paper expressly links promotion with encouraging workers to perform and enhance productivity.

questions.question: According to the 2026 paper, certain professionals must pass a compulsory examination before promotion to—
questions.explanation: PSR 070301 is cited as requiring other professionals to pass the examination before promotion to GL 14.

questions.question: The compulsory examination provision referred to above is found under—
questions.explanation: The source specifically identifies PSR 070301.

questions.question: The standard of discipline expected of staff is set out primarily in—
options: rules and regulations of the Service
questions.explanation: The 2025 paper states that disciplinary standards are contained in the rules and regulations of the Service.

questions.question: Administrative action in government is bound by rules to ensure—
questions.explanation: These three purposes are expressly stated.

questions.question: The PSRs are described in the paper as the basic—
options: condition of service for public servants
questions.explanation: The paper calls the PSRs the basic condition of service for public servants.

questions.question: Why are circulars sometimes issued to amend PSR provisions?
options: Because government practice changes and rules may need amendment.
Because PSRs have no legal relevance.
Because every officer can rewrite a PSR.
Because circulars automatically override the Constitution.
questions.explanation: The paper explains that circulars and circular letters amend some provisions of the PSRs and should specify the rules amended.

questions.question: A circular amending a PSR provision should specifically state—
options: the aspect(s)/number(s) of the rule amended
the names of all civil servants
questions.explanation: The 2025 paper expressly requires the amended aspect or rule number to be stated.

questions.question: Fair hearing in personnel management requires personnel matters to be—
options: placed before the appropriate management committee for consideration
decided privately by the immediate supervisor
ignored if the officer denies wrongdoing
questions.explanation: The paper says every personnel matter should be placed before the appropriate staff-management committee.

questions.question: According to the 2026 paper, which are identified as basic elements of fair hearing in staff discipline?
questions.explanation: The paper emphasizes fair hearing, with queries and replies described as a basic fundamental right.

questions.question: A personnel manager believes an allegation against an officer has merit and therefore refuses to place it before the appropriate committee. Which principle is compromised?
questions.explanation: The fair-hearing principle applies whether or not the personnel manager believes the matter has merit; it must be considered by the appropriate committee.

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as a serious misconduct category?
questions.explanation: Falsification of records appears in the listed serious misconduct categories.

questions.question: Which action is identified as misconduct in the source?
questions.explanation: Withholding files is expressly listed among the misconduct categories.

questions.question: Absence from duty without leave or permission is identified as—
questions.explanation: It is expressly included in the misconduct list.

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as misconduct?
questions.explanation: False claims against government appear in the source's misconduct list.

questions.question: Engaging in partisan political activities is identified in the paper as—
questions.explanation: It is expressly listed among misconduct categories.

questions.question: Which financial condition is listed as misconduct?
questions.explanation: Bankruptcy/serious financial embarrassment is included in the list.

questions.question: Unauthorized disclosure of an official document is—
questions.explanation: Unauthorized disclosure of an official document appears in the misconduct list.

questions.question: Which pair consists entirely of listed misconduct categories?
questions.explanation: Both bribery and corruption are expressly listed.

questions.question: Which of the following is specifically listed?
questions.explanation: Embezzlement appears in the misconduct list.

questions.question: Violation of the Oath of Secrecy is identified as—
questions.explanation: Violation of the Oath of Secrecy is expressly listed.

questions.question: Which action is identified as prejudicial to State security?
options: An action prejudicial to the Security of the State
questions.explanation: “Action prejudicial to the Security of the State” is listed among misconduct categories.

questions.question: Advance Fee Fraud is identified in the source by reference to—
questions.explanation: The misconduct list identifies Advance Fee Fraud as Criminal Code 419.

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as misconduct?
questions.explanation: Nepotism or any other form of preferential treatment is listed.

questions.question: Divided loyalty is identified as—
questions.explanation: Divided loyalty appears in the misconduct list.

questions.question: Which of the following appears in the source's misconduct list?
questions.explanation: Sabotage is expressly listed.

questions.question: Willful damage to public property is treated in the source as—
questions.explanation: It appears among the listed misconduct categories.

questions.question: Which conduct is expressly included in the misconduct list?
questions.explanation: Sexual harassment is specifically listed.

questions.question: Cyber Crime is treated in the paper as—
questions.explanation: Cyber Crime appears in the listed misconduct categories.

questions.question: The phrase “any other act unbecoming of a Public Officer” is—
questions.explanation: The phrase appears as the final listed misconduct category.

questions.question: Training is intended primarily to help staff develop better—
questions.explanation: The paper says training develops better skills, knowledge and attitude for effective and efficient performance.

questions.question: Which is a short training programme identified in the paper?
questions.explanation: Induction courses, job-improvement courses and seminars are identified as short training programmes.

questions.question: Establishment Circular No. 1/2004 provides for—
options: in-service training, study leave with pay, study leave without pay and public service awards
recruitment, promotion, discipline and retirement only
questions.explanation: Those four training/development provisions are expressly identified.

questions.question: In-service training is sponsored by the—
options: Department of Establishments in tertiary institutions
questions.explanation: The source identifies the Department of Establishments as sponsor of in-service training in tertiary institutions.

questions.question: The State Civil Service Training Centre plays an important role in training—
options: officers in the training grade and middle manpower requirements
questions.explanation: That is its stated role in the paper.

questions.question: Technical Assistance Schemes are identified as another means of—
questions.explanation: The paper identifies Technical Assistance Schemes arranged by foreign bodies and government as another training sponsorship route.

questions.question: Why does government train its workforce according to the paper?
options: To expose officers to modern and contemporary techniques and skills
To prevent officers from being promoted
questions.explanation: This is the stated rationale for government workforce training.

questions.question: Officers on study leave with pay continue to receive—
questions.explanation: The paper states that officers on study leave with pay receive salaries during the course.

questions.question: The normal duration stated for study leave with pay should not exceed—
questions.explanation: The source states that the course should not normally be more than four years, though exceptional approval may be granted.

questions.question: Study leave without pay is intended for officers who may not benefit from—
options: in-service training, study leave with pay or public service award
questions.explanation: That is the stated context for study leave without pay.

questions.question: Study leave without pay is intended to enable officers to—
options: acquire knowledge or sharpen their skills
questions.explanation: The paper gives acquiring knowledge and sharpening skills as its purpose.

questions.question: The procedure for part-time study is contained in—
questions.explanation: The paper cites Establishment Circular No. 6 of 1999 dated 23 July 1999.

questions.question: The paper states that the approved part-time study procedure contains approximately—
questions.explanation: The source says there are about eight steps and guidelines.

questions.question: Induction and orientation programmes are described as part of—
questions.explanation: The paper identifies induction and orientation as part of government training.

questions.question: New staff are generally exposed to the workings of government through—
questions.explanation: The source states that after recruitment, new staff are exposed to government operations through induction and orientation.

questions.question: Which is NOT listed as an expectation emphasized during induction?
questions.explanation: Loyalty, punctuality and attendance are listed; political campaigning is not.

questions.question: Induction emphasizes obedience to—
questions.explanation: Obedience to constituted authority is expressly listed.

questions.question: Which of the following is included in induction expectations?
questions.explanation: Avoidance of conflict of interest is specifically included.

questions.question: Which combination contains only induction expectations identified in the paper?
options: Loyalty, punctuality, honesty and sense of responsibility
Profit maximization, competition, lobbying and campaigning
questions.explanation: All four are expressly listed under induction/orientation.

questions.question: Induction emphasizes an officer's relationship with—
options: the public and others at the workstation
questions.explanation: Relationship with the public and with others in the workstation is specifically listed.

questions.question: General efficiency and productivity are identified as—
questions.explanation: General efficiency and productivity appear among induction expectations.

questions.question: Keeping the Oath of Secrecy is emphasized during—
questions.explanation: Keeping the Oath of Secrecy is expressly listed among induction expectations.

questions.question: An officer who attends induction but continues to disregard punctuality and attendance has failed to observe—
questions.explanation: Punctuality and attendance are specifically identified expectations

questions.question: Performance appraisal is the process of—
questions.explanation: The 2026 paper defines staff performance appraisal as the process of ascertaining staff productivity.

questions.question: Which is NOT identified as a benefit of performance appraisal?
questions.explanation: The paper identifies productivity, promotion, training and job deployment as benefits.

questions.question: PSR 060301 provides for yearly completion of—
questions.explanation: The source identifies PSR 060301 as providing for annual APER completion.

questions.question: APER should be administered—
options: only to officers mature for promotion
only to officers due for retirement
to all officers at the end of each calendar year
questions.explanation: The paper expressly says APER should be administered to all officers at the end of each calendar year regardless of promotion eligibility.

questions.question: The primary purpose of APER is to build a full record of an officer's—
questions.explanation: APER builds a record from which suitability for promotion may be judged.

questions.question: APER can help the Reporting Officer identify—
questions.explanation: The source specifically identifies strengths and weaknesses as an APER function.

questions.question: Identified weaknesses in APER may be used to determine an officer's—
questions.explanation: Reporting Officers use identified strengths and weaknesses to determine training needs.

questions.question: APER may also assist in assigning an officer—
options: to a new or specific job
questions.explanation: APER is described as a tool for assigning an officer to a new or specific job to enhance performance.

questions.question: An officer is not yet eligible for promotion. The supervisor decides not to complete APER. According to the paper, this is—
questions.explanation: APER should be completed for all officers whether or not they are mature or eligible for promotion.

questions.question: Target setting is described as a process of improving performance through—
questions.explanation: The paper defines target setting around planned, goal-directed activities with steps and measurements.

questions.question: Which is an element of target setting?
questions.explanation: Quantity of output demanded is one of the listed target-setting terms.

questions.question: Which target-setting element concerns the standard of work expected?
questions.explanation: Quality of output demanded is expressly listed.

questions.question: Target setting considers the amount of—
options: resources to be utilized for a given output
questions.explanation: Resource utilization for a given quantity of output is one of the listed elements.

questions.question: Which target-setting element deals with the period within which output is expected?
questions.explanation: Time span of output is expressly listed.

questions.question: “Manner of performance” is included among—
questions.explanation: It is one of the six target-setting elements listed.

questions.question: Target setting also considers—
questions.explanation: Constraints/solutions to problems are the final listed target-setting element.

questions.question: The word “Ethics” is derived from the Greek word—
questions.explanation: The paper states that ethics is derived from the Greek word ethos, meaning character or custom.

questions.question: The Latin word “Mos” is associated in the paper with—
questions.explanation: The paper connects Mos with morality and customs.

questions.question: Ethics and morality describe what a society or group believes to be—
questions.explanation: This is the paper's stated description.

questions.question: Which of the following is an element of ethics listed in the source?
questions.explanation: Integrity is explicitly listed among the elements of ethics.

questions.question: Which pair contains only ethical elements identified in the paper?
questions.explanation: Honesty and trustworthiness appear in the ethics list; the other pairs are misconduct categories.

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as an element of ethics?
questions.explanation: Accountability is one of the listed ethical elements.

questions.question: Which ethical element most directly relates to treating people respectfully?
questions.explanation: Courtesy is expressly included in the ethics list.

questions.question: Which pair is most consistent with the ethics list?
questions.explanation: Teamwork and cooperation are listed ethical elements.

questions.question: Which of the following is identified as an ethical element?
questions.explanation: Neutrality appears among the ethical elements.

questions.question: Professionalism is presented in the paper as—
questions.explanation: Professionalism is included in the ethics list.

questions.question: Communication in personnel management is described as the process of—
options: conveying, disseminating or receiving information, messages, data or directives
questions.explanation: That is the definition provided in the 2026 paper.

questions.question: The desired flow of communication in an organization should occur—
options: from top down, down to top and to the public
questions.explanation: The paper identifies communication flow from top to bottom, bottom to top and to the public.

questions.question: In the communication process, the person who interprets the message is the—
questions.explanation: The source describes the sender initiating the message and the receiver interpreting, understanding and acting/reacting to it.

questions.question: The paper advises officers to follow the established—
questions.explanation: Officers are advised to communicate through the established line of command.

questions.question: A junior officer wishes to communicate a personnel matter to a senior echelon. According to the paper, the communication should generally pass—
options: through the immediate superior and upper echelon
questions.explanation: The source describes communication from the officer to the immediate superior and then upward through the echelon.

questions.question: Which is a method of written communication in personnel administration?
questions.explanation: Official correspondence, letters and endorsements are specifically listed.

questions.question: Which of the following is included among written communication methods?
questions.explanation: Minuting in files and brief is expressly listed.

questions.question: Reports, memoranda and addresses/speeches are classified in the paper as—
questions.explanation: They appear in the list of written communication methods.

questions.question: Which pair consists entirely of written communication methods listed in the source?
options: Minutes of meetings and file notes/enclosures
questions.explanation: Both minutes of meetings and file notes/enclosures are listed.

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as a Public Service career record?
questions.explanation: The 2026 paper lists the letter of first appointment among career records.

questions.question: Which record contains the officer's personal/confidential information?
questions.explanation: Personal/confidential files are expressly listed as career records.

questions.question: Which record establishes medical fitness in the listed career records?
questions.explanation: A medical report of fitness is expressly listed.

questions.question: Which document is listed as evidence relating to age?
questions.explanation: Birth certificate or age declaration appears in the career-record list.

questions.question: The record of service should be updated with—
questions.explanation: The source specifically notes record of service updated with next of kin.

questions.question: Which record demonstrates that an officer's appointment has been confirmed?
questions.explanation: Confirmation of appointment letter is expressly listed.

questions.question: Which performance-related record appears in the career-record list?
questions.explanation: Annual Performance Evaluation Report is included among career records.

questions.question: Which document records an officer's advancement through promotion?
questions.explanation: Promotion letters are specifically listed.

questions.question: Which records relate specifically to further education or staff development?
questions.explanation: Study leave/In-service Training letters are listed career records.

questions.question: Which of the following is a career record relating to absence from duty?
questions.explanation: Leave letters are included in the career-record list.

questions.question: Which record relates directly to an officer's movement within the Service?
questions.explanation: Posting letters are included among career records.

questions.question: Which document is specifically associated with salary administration in the career records?
questions.explanation: The last pay certificate is listed among career records.

questions.question: Which of the following appears in the source's career-record list?
questions.explanation: Credentials are explicitly listed.

questions.question: Which record relates to a change in an officer's personal identity information?
questions.explanation: Letter of change of name appears in the listed records.

questions.question: Which of the following is among the additional career records identified in the paper?
questions.explanation: Tax records are explicitly listed.

questions.question: Which record relates to an officer's financial obligation?
questions.explanation: Records of indebtedness are included among the career records.

questions.question: Which record concerns health-related absence?
questions.explanation: Sick leave records are expressly listed.

questions.question: According to the paper, career records are important because officers should—
options: preserve and keep custody of them as they progress in the Service
questions.explanation: The paper expressly emphasizes their importance and the officer's responsibility to preserve and custody them.

questions.question: Which is identified as a source of personnel-management information?
options: 2022 Edition of Akwa Ibom State Public Service Rules
questions.explanation: The 2026 paper lists the 2022 PSR among sources of information.

questions.question: Which record-management source is specifically listed?
options: 2014 Edition of Akwa Ibom State Handbook on Records Management
questions.explanation: The 2014 State Handbook on Records Management is listed.

questions.question: The Constitution listed as a source of personnel information is the—
questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution as amended is expressly listed.

questions.question: Which financial instrument is identified as a personnel-management information source?
questions.explanation: Financial Instruction appears in the source list.

questions.question: Which of the following is identified as an official source of personnel information?
questions.explanation: Treasury circulars are expressly listed.

questions.question: Reports of Commissions of Enquiry are classified in the paper as—
questions.explanation: They appear in the source-of-information list.

questions.question: Government White Papers are identified as—
questions.explanation: Government White Papers are expressly listed among sources of information

questions.question: CSC Circular No. 1/2000 deals with guidelines for—
options: appointment, promotion, discipline and transfer of officers
questions.explanation: The 2026 paper identifies those four subjects for CSC Circular No. 1/2000.

questions.question: CSC Circular No. 1/2007 introduced—
options: Special Promotion and its management machinery
questions.explanation: The source identifies CSC Circular No. 1/2007 as introducing Special Promotion and its management machinery.

questions.question: CSC Circular No. 1/2008 concerns guidelines on—
options: conversion/transfer/appointment into the administrative officers cadre
questions.explanation: That is the subject attributed to CSC Circular No. 1/2008.

questions.question: HCS Circular No. 3/2010 concerns conversion using—
options: certificates/diplomas obtained before joining the Service
questions.explanation: The circular is identified as concerning conversion using certificates/diplomas obtained before joining the Service.

questions.question: HCS Circular No. 6/2010 concerns—
options: leave of absence to participate in politics
questions.explanation: That is the subject stated for HCS Circular No. 6/2010.

questions.question: Establishment Circular No. 5/2011 addresses—
questions.explanation: The paper identifies that subject for Establishment Circular No. 5/2011.

questions.question: Establishment Circular No. 15/2020 clarifies—
questions.explanation: The paper describes it as clarification on barring and change of cadres as an additional general rule to PSR 070103.

questions.question: CSC Circular No. 2/2014 is associated with guidelines on—
questions.explanation: It clarifies paragraph 23 of CSC Circular No. 1/2000 concerning conversion.

questions.question: Establishment Circular No. 10/2019 concerns placement involving—
questions.explanation: The paper identifies its subject as placement on appointment with NYSC exemption/exclusion and discharge certificates.

questions.question: A GL 05 officer has a personnel complaint and wants to write directly to the Governor. Which action is most consistent with the seminar?
options: Write directly to the Governor because personnel matters are confidential.
Pass the matter through the relevant management committee.
questions.explanation: The paper expressly states that officers should not write directly to the Head of Service or Governor on personnel matters without passing through the relevant management committees.

questions.question: A GL 09 officer is involved in a personnel matter. The Ministry sends it to the JSC because the officer is not a political appointee. Which is the problem?
options: JSC handles GL 01–06, while SSMC handles GL 07–17.
questions.explanation: The JSC handles GL 01–06, while the SSMC handles GL 07–17.

questions.question: A probationary pensionable officer completes two years but does nothing about confirmation. What risk does the paper identify?
questions.explanation: The source warns that failure to secure confirmation after two years may result in future stagnation.

questions.question: A supervisor completes APER only for officers who are promotion-eligible. Which statement is correct?
options: The approach is consistent with the source.
The approach is inconsistent because APER applies to all officers annually.
APER applies only to GL 07 and above.
questions.explanation: The source expressly requires APER for all officers at the end of each calendar year, regardless of promotion maturity.

questions.question: An APER reveals that an officer has a weakness in a particular technical area. The Reporting Officer should primarily use that information to—
options: change the officer's salary grade immediately
questions.explanation: The paper says strengths and weaknesses identified through APER can be used to determine training needs.

questions.question: A Department sets a target but gives no quantity, quality, time frame or resource expectation. Which conclusion BEST follows the source?
options: Target setting requires only a job title.
Targets are concerned only with employee age.
questions.explanation: Quantity, quality, resources and time span are among the specified target-setting elements.

questions.question: A new officer receives induction but is told nothing about loyalty, punctuality, public relations or conflict of interest. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
options: Important induction expectations identified in the seminar have been omitted.
The officer has completed every relevant induction requirement.
Those issues belong only to financial management.
questions.explanation: Loyalty, punctuality, relationship with the public and avoidance of conflict of interest are expressly listed induction expectations.

questions.question: A Ministry wants to fill a GL 09 vacancy but ignores the Scheme of Service because a candidate is personally recommended. Which source principle is violated?
options: The Scheme of Service should be strictly adhered to in filling vacancies.
Recommendations automatically override the Scheme of Service.
The JSC must approve every GL 09 appointment.
questions.explanation: The 2025 paper specifically requires strict adherence to the Scheme of Service when filling existing vacancies.

questions.question: An officer is accused of misconduct. The personnel manager believes the allegation is obviously true and wants to punish the officer immediately without committee consideration. Which principle is most directly violated?
questions.explanation: Personnel matters, whether considered meritorious or not, should be placed before the appropriate committee for deliberation and recommendation.

questions.question: A GL 04 officer is promoted by the CSC while a GL 12 officer is promoted by a Permanent Secretary under the delegation described in the source. Which assessment is correct?
options: Both actions are consistent with the source.
Only the GL 04 action is consistent.
Only the GL 12 action is consistent.
questions.explanation: The source states that GL 01–06 promotion is delegated to Permanent Secretaries/Heads of Department, while the CSC promotes GL 07 and above.

questions.question: A newly recruited officer: has the required Scheme-of-Service qualification; is within the stated age range; has the required medical certification and NYSC documentation; receives a probationary pensionable appointment; completes induction; undergoes annual APER; is trained where weaknesses are identified; communicates through the established line of command; maintains proper career records; and becomes subject to discipline through the applicable rules and fair-hearing process. Which statement BEST captures the Personnel Management framework presented in the uploaded papers?
options: Personnel Management ends once an officer is recruited.
Personnel Management is a continuous process covering acquisition, utilization, development, motivation, protection, performance, records, communication and discipline.
Personnel Management concerns only salaries and promotions.
Personnel Management is primarily the responsibility of the Civil Service Commission and excludes line managers.
questions.explanation: The papers present Personnel Management as a broad and continuing function encompassing acquisition/utilization of human resources, training and development, motivation, protection, performance appraisal, records, communication and discipline. They also emphasize that managers throughout the Service perform personnel functions.

questions.question: A Reporting Officer argues that an officer who is not yet eligible for promotion does not need an APER for the current year because the report cannot immediately affect promotion. Which response is MOST consistent with the seminar material?
options: Correct, because APER exists primarily for promotion.
Correct, unless the officer has a training need.
Incorrect, because APER is to be administered to officers at the end of each calendar year regardless of promotion eligibility.
Incorrect only where the officer has spent at least three years on the grade.
questions.explanation: The material expressly states that APER should be administered to all officers at the end of each calendar year whether or not the officer is mature or eligible for promotion. APER also serves training and job-deployment purposes, so restricting it to promotion-eligible officers would be too narrow.

questions.question: An officer's APER reveals a recurring weakness in a particular technical area. The Reporting Officer wants to use that information to improve the officer rather than merely record the weakness. What is the most directly supported next step?
options: Transfer the officer to another Ministry.
questions.explanation: The source specifically states that strengths and weaknesses identified through APER are used by the Reporting Officer to determine the officer's training needs. A weakness is therefore not automatically a disciplinary matter.

questions.question: A supervisor gives an officer a target of “produce as many reports as possible,” but provides no expected standard of quality. Which element of target setting has been most obviously omitted?
questions.explanation: The source identifies both quantity and quality of output as separate elements of target setting. Saying “as many as possible” addresses quantity but does not establish the required standard of quality.

questions.question: A Director tells an officer: “Complete 40 verified applications within four weeks, using the available staff and equipment, and follow the approved procedure.” Which target-setting element is represented by “within four weeks”?
questions.explanation: The source separately identifies time span of output as one of the six elements of target setting. “Within four weeks” specifies the period within which the expected output must be achieved.

questions.question: A supervisor gives an officer responsibility for producing a specified number of outputs but fails to identify what staff, equipment or other resources may be used. Which target-setting element is missing?
options: Amount of resources to be utilized
questions.explanation: The source identifies the amount of resources to be utilized for a given quantity of output as a distinct target-setting element.

questions.question: An officer consistently produces the required quantity within the stipulated period but does so through a method that violates the required procedure. Which target-setting element is most directly implicated?
questions.explanation: Target setting is not merely about how much and how quickly. The source specifically includes manner of performance, meaning the way the work is expected to be carried out.

questions.question: A manager identifies a recurring obstacle preventing an officer from achieving a target and develops a practical way of overcoming it. This corresponds most closely to which target-setting element?
questions.explanation: “Constraints/solutions to problems” is expressly listed as one of the six elements of target setting. The scenario concerns identifying an obstacle and addressing it.

questions.question: Two officers produce the same quantity of work within the same period. Officer X follows the required procedure; Officer Y achieves the result by ignoring the prescribed process. If their targets properly included all relevant dimensions, which element would most clearly distinguish them?
questions.explanation: The source identifies manner of performance separately from quantity, quality, resources and time. Thus, identical output does not necessarily mean identical performance.

questions.question: A personnel manager personally believes an officer's petition is weak. The manager therefore decides that the matter does not deserve consideration by any personnel-management committee. Which principle in the seminar does this approach violate?
questions.explanation: The principle of fair hearing requires all personnel matters, whether or not the personnel manager considers them meritorious, to be placed before the appropriate personnel-management committee for deliberation and recommendation to the final approving body.

questions.question: A personnel officer says: “I have already decided what should happen to this officer, so there is no need for the committee to deliberate.” What is the strongest objection based on the source?
options: Committees exist only for promotion matters.
Final approving bodies must always accept the personnel officer's decision.
Personnel matters should be considered by the appropriate committee before appropriate recommendations are made to the final approving body.
Personnel officers have no role whatsoever in personnel decisions.
questions.explanation: The source does not say personnel officers have no role. Rather, it establishes a deliberative process: the matter goes before the appropriate personnel-management committee, which considers it and makes appropriate recommendations to the final approving body.

questions.question: Which situation BEST illustrates the difference between training and education as defined in the seminar?
options: An officer learns a specific skill needed for a particular assignment, while another acquires formal background knowledge in a course.
An officer is disciplined for misconduct, while another is promoted.
An officer is transferred, while another is retired.
An officer receives an APER, while another receives a salary adjustment.
questions.explanation: The source defines training as acquiring knowledge, skills and attitude to be applied at a particular assignment, while education is acquiring formal background knowledge of a subject or course.

questions.question: An officer attends a structured programme specifically designed to improve his skills and job experience in his current position. Which concept fits the source most precisely?
questions.explanation: The source defines development as a planned set of actions designed to improve the skills and job experience of an individual in their current position.

questions.question: An officer undertakes a university course to acquire formal background knowledge of a subject. Which classification is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Education is specifically defined as the process of acquiring formal background knowledge of a subject or course.

questions.question: Which statement would be least accurate according to the seminar's definitions?
options: Training may be linked to a particular assignment.
Development concerns improving skills and job experience in the current position.
Education is limited to practical skills needed for a particular government assignment.
Education involves formal background knowledge of a subject or course.
questions.explanation: This reverses the source's distinction. Training, rather than education, is defined around knowledge, skills and attitude to be applied at a particular assignment. Education concerns formal background knowledge.

questions.question: An officer who cannot benefit from in-service training, study leave with pay or a public service award wants to acquire additional knowledge or sharpen existing skills. Which provision most directly fits the source?
questions.explanation: The seminar states that study leave without pay is intended for officers who may not benefit from in-service training, study leave with pay or public service awards, enabling them to acquire knowledge and/or sharpen their skills.

questions.question: An officer is approved for study leave with pay. Which statement is most consistent with the seminar?
options: The officer must stop receiving salary during the course.
The officer receives salary during the course, normally for a period not exceeding four years.
The officer is automatically promoted after completing the course.
The officer must convert the leave into secondment.
questions.explanation: The source states that officers on study leave with pay continue to receive their salaries during the course, which should normally not exceed four years, although exceptional approval may cover longer courses.

questions.question: A newly recruited officer is being introduced to government expectations. The programme emphasizes loyalty, punctuality, honesty, relationship with the public, avoidance of conflict of interest and keeping the Oath of Secrecy. What is the BEST classification?
questions.explanation: These are expressly listed among the expectations emphasized during induction and orientation after recruitment.

questions.question: A new officer is punctual but repeatedly ignores constituted authority and shows little sense of responsibility. Which conclusion is most defensible from the induction material?
options: Punctuality alone satisfies the induction expectations.
The officer satisfies the requirements because attendance is sufficient.
The officer is meeting only some of the expectations; obedience to constituted authority and responsibility are also emphasized.
These matters are relevant only to political office holders.
questions.explanation: The source lists punctuality, attendance, obedience to constituted authority, honesty, sense of responsibility and commitment, among other expectations. Meeting one does not erase failure in others.

questions.question: A Director wants to prevent idleness and truancy while also establishing an objective basis for evaluating staff performance. Which administrative measure is most directly supported?
options: Give every officer a Schedule of Duties clearly spelling out expected work.
Wait until promotion is due before assigning duties.
Assess officers primarily according to how busy they appear.
questions.explanation: The seminar recommends that everyone in the office should have a Schedule of Duties clearly stating what the officer is expected to do. It links this to preventing idleness and truancy and to more objective assessment.

questions.question: A supervisor prepares a detailed Schedule of Duties for an officer and later discovers that the officer worked extremely hard but delivered results below the required standard. Which principle from the seminar should guide the supervisor's assessment?
options: Effort and result should be treated as identical.
Result should never be considered if effort was high.
The supervisor should distinguish between effort and result when assigning and assessing responsibility.
The Schedule of Duties becomes irrelevant once the officer has made an effort.
questions.explanation: The seminar explicitly advises managers to let officers know the difference between effort and result when assigning responsibility. A high level of effort does not automatically establish effective delivery against the expected duties.

questions.question: A newly appointed officer argues that “personnel management” concerns only recruitment because once an officer has been employed, the personnel function has effectively ended. Which response is MOST consistent with the seminar?
options: Correct; recruitment is the central and practically complete personnel function.
Incorrect; personnel management also encompasses utilization, training, development, motivation, discipline, retirement and related functions.
Correct, except where the officer is on Grade Level 14 and above.
Incorrect only because personnel management also includes procurement of office equipment.
questions.explanation: The source defines personnel management broadly as dealing with the acquisition and utilization of human beings to accomplish organizational objectives. It further associates management with recruitment, training, development, remuneration, motivation, communication, discipline, retirement and other personnel activities.

questions.question: An MDA is experiencing poor productivity because officers are being assigned duties without proper coordination, while employee welfare is also being neglected. Which underlying objective of human resource management is MOST directly implicated?
options: Achieving optimum productivity while satisfying the needs of employees, employer and other stakeholders
Transferring personnel functions entirely to the Civil Service Commission
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies the essence of human resource management as achieving optimum productivity while satisfying the needs of the employee, employer and stakeholders such as the public.

questions.question: Which of the following represents deployment rather than procurement in personnel management?
options: Assigning an officer responsibility for a particular function and posting the officer accordingly
questions.explanation: The source describes deployment as the designation of officers, assignment of responsibilities and posting, while procurement includes staff recruitment and material purchases.

questions.question: A Ministry has a recurring personnel problem that existing policy does not adequately address. The Personnel Directorate decides to draft a new policy specifically to deal with the problem. Which Personnel Directorate function is being performed?
questions.explanation: Policy initiation and formulation involves proposing and drafting new personnel policies or revisions to address recurring or anticipated problems.

questions.question: A Personnel Directorate advises a line Directorate on the proper interpretation and coordination of applicable rules, circulars and guidelines. This is best classified as—
questions.explanation: The source specifically describes the Advice function as giving direction and coordination concerning rules, regulations, circulars and guidelines.

questions.question: Which situation BEST illustrates the control function of personnel management?
options: Drafting a new policy to address an anticipated personnel problem
Monitoring employees to ensure conformity with established personnel policies, procedures and practices
questions.explanation: Control involves monitoring employee performance to ensure conformity with established personnel policies, procedures and practices.

questions.question: A line Directorate complains that the Personnel Directorate is interfering with its operational work. The Personnel Director responds that its role is to help the operating Directorate perform more effectively and efficiently. Which description from the seminar BEST supports the Personnel Director?
options: The Personnel Directorate exists primarily to replace line Directorates.
The Personnel Directorate operates in an auxiliary and advisory role that facilitates relationships with other Directorates.
Personnel Directorates have exclusive responsibility for every operational function of an MDA.
Personnel Directorates are independent of line Directorates.
questions.explanation: The source expressly describes Personnel Directorates as operating in an auxiliary advisory role, facilitating relationships with other Directorates and helping line/operating Directorates work more effectively and efficiently.

questions.question: According to the seminar, the Personnel Directorate is created partly to sustain—
options: specialized talent, knowledge, coordination and standardization
questions.explanation: The source specifically identifies specialized talent, knowledge, coordination and standardization as purposes associated with the staff Directorate structure.

questions.question: An officer claims that because the Civil Service Commission deals with personnel matters, it therefore automatically has authority over every person working anywhere within the wider State Public Service. Which answer is MOST consistent with the seminar?
options: Correct; the CSC controls every employee in the State Public Service without distinction.
Correct only for officers on Grade Level 07 and above.
Incorrect; the material distinguishes the State Civil Service from the wider State Public Service, with various Commissions, Boards, Parastatals and Agencies appointing Public Service employees.
Incorrect because the CSC has no personnel powers whatsoever.
questions.explanation: The source makes an important distinction: the CSC has powers concerning employees in the State Civil Service, while persons in the wider Public Service may be appointed by various Commissions, Boards, Parastatals and Agencies.

questions.question: Which of the following powers is expressly attributed to the State Civil Service Commission in the seminar?
options: Appointing persons to offices in the State Civil Service and exercising disciplinary control over them
Appointing every worker in the State Public Service
questions.explanation: The material states that the State Civil Service Commission has constitutional power to appoint persons to offices in the State Civil Service and dismiss and exercise disciplinary control over persons holding those offices.

questions.question: A personnel officer says, “Since I am responsible for personnel administration, I am the only person who can properly be described as a personnel manager.” Which response best reflects the seminar?
options: Correct; personnel management is restricted to designated administrative officers.
Incorrect; anyone who manages people and resources in the day-to-day running of an organization performs personnel-management functions.
Incorrect only because every civil servant automatically becomes a personnel officer.
questions.explanation: The source makes a distinction between designated personnel officers and the broader practical meaning of personnel manager. Anyone involved in the day-to-day management of people and resources may perform personnel-management functions.

questions.question: A Head of Section supervises several employees, assigns their duties and manages their day-to-day work. Even though the officer is not formally designated as a Personnel Officer, the seminar would regard the officer as—
options: a personnel manager in the practical sense
a member of the Civil Service Commission
an officer whose role is limited to procurement
questions.explanation: The seminar states that officers who have people working under them and who deal with people and resources in day-to-day management perform personnel-management functions and are therefore personnel managers in that practical sense.

questions.question: Which of the following combinations contains only basic tools for personnel management identified in the seminar?
options: Public Service Rules, Circulars, Schemes of Service, Annual Appropriation Laws and Financial Regulation
APER, newspaper editorials, political manifestos and court judgments
Circulars, private contracts, party constitutions and staff petitions
Financial Regulation, personal diaries, newspapers and election results
questions.explanation: The source expressly identifies the Public Service Rules, Circulars, Schemes of Service, Annual Appropriation Laws and Financial Regulation as basic tools governing day-to-day personnel administration.

questions.question: The seminar says the Public Service Rules do more than merely prescribe duties. Which statement BEST captures this broader role?
options: They provide guidance to public servants while also stating government powers and responsibilities and securing officers' rights and privileges.
They exist primarily to determine the political leadership of Ministries.
They are concerned only with disciplinary offences.
They replace all other personnel-management instruments.
questions.explanation: The source says the PSRs provide guidance for staff in performing their duties and responsibilities and secure public servants' rights and privileges by clearly stating government powers and responsibilities as employer.

questions.question: An officer receives an instruction from a superior and immediately forwards it to the public without first following the organization's established communication route. Which principle in the seminar has most clearly been disregarded?
options: Established line of command or communication
questions.explanation: The communication section advises officers to follow the established line of command or communication, moving through the immediate superior and appropriate upper echelon rather than bypassing the established route.

questions.question: A departmental message moves from a junior officer to the immediate superior, then to the appropriate upper echelon, while relevant information is also communicated to the public. Which conception of communication does this BEST demonstrate?
options: Effective communication involves information flow downward, upward and to the public.
Communication is restricted to written correspondence.
questions.explanation: The source states that successful communication should facilitate the flow of information from the top down, from the bottom up and to the public.

questions.question: A departmental officer prepares an official memorandum, while another records decisions reached during a meeting. Which classification BEST applies?
options: Both are forms of written communication in personnel administration.
The memorandum is personnel utilization while the minutes are control.
The memorandum is oral communication while the minutes are deployment.
Neither constitutes personnel communication unless approved by the CSC.
questions.explanation: The source lists reports, memoranda and addresses/speeches, as well as minutes of meetings, among the methods of written communication in personnel administration.

questions.question: An officer receives a directive but interprets it incorrectly and consequently acts contrary to what the sender intended. According to the seminar's description of communication, which stage has most directly failed?
options: The receiver's interpretation and understanding of the message
The establishment of the Personnel Directorate
questions.explanation: The source describes communication as involving a sender initiating a message and a receiver who interprets it, understands it and acts or reacts to it. The scenario identifies a failure at the receiver's interpretation/understanding stage.

questions.question: A senior officer is honest, punctual and highly competent but deliberately uses his official position to favour relatives over equally qualified candidates. Which ethical element is most directly undermined by this conduct?
questions.explanation: The personnel seminar explicitly identifies nepotism or preferential treatment as serious misconduct. It also lists neutrality, integrity, honesty, accountability, professionalism and other ethical values.

questions.question: A civil servant argues that an officer's personal honesty is sufficient to establish ethical conduct, even where the officer consistently disregards accountability, neutrality and professionalism. Which response is MOST faithful to the seminar's treatment of ethics?
options: Correct; honesty is the only essential ethical element.
Correct, provided the officer is senior enough.
Incorrect; the seminar presents ethics as encompassing multiple elements, including integrity, honesty, accountability, neutrality and professionalism.
Incorrect only because ethics concerns punctuality and nothing else.
questions.explanation: The seminar presents ethics as a collection of values, not a single trait. Its listed elements include integrity, honesty, trustworthiness, accountability, punctuality, probity, teamwork, neutrality and professionalism, among others

questions.question: An officer habitually arrives late to work but has not committed any of the acts listed under serious misconduct. Under the classification in the seminar, this conduct is—
questions.explanation: Habitual lateness to work is expressly listed under PSR 040301 – Wrong Doing. It is not listed there as serious misconduct.

questions.question: A senior officer deliberately suppresses an official record in order to prevent another officer from discovering its contents. Which classification is most appropriate according to the seminar?
questions.explanation: Suppression of records appears specifically under PSR 040401 – Serious Misconduct. The deliberate nature of the conduct does not change the source's classification: suppression of records is expressly listed there.

questions.question: Which pair is correctly classified according to the seminar?
options: Sleeping on duty — Serious Misconduct; bribery — Wrong Doing
Bribery — Serious Misconduct; sleeping on duty — Wrong Doing
Habitual lateness — Serious Misconduct; corruption — Wrong Doing
Insubordination — Serious Misconduct; embezzlement — Wrong Doing
questions.explanation: Sleeping on duty appears under Wrong Doing, while bribery appears under Serious Misconduct. The other combinations reverse or misclassify conduct listed in the source.

questions.question: An officer refuses to carry out a lawful instruction from a superior and argues that the instruction is optional because he disagrees with it. Based strictly on the seminar's classification, this is—
questions.explanation: Refusal to take or carry out a lawful instruction from superior officers is expressly listed under Wrong Doing. The question deliberately emphasizes lawful instruction because that is the wording used in the source.

questions.question: An officer deliberately falsifies an official record to make an administrative transaction appear to have been properly completed. Which category does the seminar place this under?
questions.explanation: Falsification of records is expressly listed under PSR 040401 – Serious Misconduct.

questions.question: Which of the following would be the strongest reason for classifying an act as serious misconduct under the material rather than merely relying on the general idea that it is “bad behaviour”?
options: It is an act expressly captured under PSR 040401.
It causes embarrassment to the officer.
The officer's colleagues dislike the conduct.
The officer has previously received a low APER score.
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically provides separate categories under PSR 040301 and PSR 040401. Classification should therefore follow the conduct identified in the applicable rule rather than subjective reactions to the officer.

questions.question: Consider the following four situations: Sleeping on duty Bribery Unauthorized removal of public records Sexual harassment Which option correctly identifies the category containing all four?
questions.explanation: Bribery and sexual harassment are expressly listed under Serious Misconduct, while unauthorized removal of public records and sleeping on duty are listed under Wrong Doing. Therefore, B is actually NOT correct if all four are required.

questions.question: Which of the following contains only conduct classified as Wrong Doing in the seminar?
options: Falsification, suppression of records and false claims
Sleeping on duty, improper dressing and failure to keep records
Sabotage, sexual harassment and cyber crime
questions.explanation: Sleeping on duty, improper dressing while on duty and failure to keep records are all listed under Wrong Doing. The other options contain acts expressly placed under Serious Misconduct.

questions.question: Which of the following contains only Serious Misconduct under the source?
options: Habitual lateness, sleeping on duty and negligence
Improper dressing, insubordination and discourteous behaviour
Refusal to accept posting, failure to keep records and dishonesty
questions.explanation: Bribery, embezzlement and misappropriation are all explicitly listed under Serious Misconduct. The remaining options contain conduct from the Wrong Doing category.

questions.question: An officer discloses an official document without authorization. He argues that because no financial loss occurred, the matter cannot constitute serious misconduct. Which response is best supported by the seminar?
options: Correct, because serious misconduct requires financial loss.
Correct, unless the officer is a senior officer.
Incorrect, because unauthorized disclosure of an official document is expressly listed as serious misconduct.
Incorrect only if the disclosure involved classified information.
questions.explanation: Unauthorized disclosure of official document is expressly listed under Serious Misconduct. The source does not make financial loss a condition for that classification.

questions.question: Which disciplinary measure most directly involves taking money from an officer as an imposed financial liability?
questions.explanation: Surcharge is expressly listed among the disciplinary measures available against a defaulting officer. The other options are disciplinary measures too, but they do not specifically represent the financial liability described by the term surcharge.

questions.question: An officer is absent from his duty post without authority. The disciplinary measure specifically described as non-payment for the corresponding days is—
questions.explanation: The seminar defines loss of pay/non-payment as non-payment for the corresponding days an officer is not at his duty post/station without authority.

questions.question: Which disciplinary measure affects an officer's rank, rather than merely salary or increment?
questions.explanation: The source separately identifies reduction in rank, reduction in salary, and withholding/deferment of increment. They are therefore not interchangeable measures.

questions.question: Which option contains only disciplinary measures expressly listed in the seminar?
options: Surcharge, written warning, reduction in rank
questions.explanation: Surcharge, written warning and reduction in rank all appear in the listed disciplinary measures.

questions.question: An officer receives a written warning for misconduct. Which statement is most accurate?
options: A written warning is not disciplinary because it does not affect salary.
A written warning is one of the disciplinary measures identified in the seminar.
A written warning automatically amounts to dismissal.
A written warning is equivalent to study leave without pay.
questions.explanation: Written warning is expressly listed among the disciplinary measures that may be taken against a defaulting officer.

questions.question: An officer goes on maternity leave. Her supervisor proposes continuing disciplinary proceedings throughout the period because “disciplinary matters have nothing to do with maternity.” What does the source specifically provide?
options: Disciplinary proceedings are automatically converted into dismissal.
Disciplinary proceedings are postponed under the maternity provisions.
Maternity leave cancels all disciplinary records.
questions.explanation: The source expressly identifies postponement of disciplinary proceedings among the maternity provisions under PSR 030301–030304.

questions.question: According to the seminar, the authorized absence from duty for maternity leave is—
questions.explanation: The source specifically states sixteen weeks as the authorized maternity leave absence.

questions.question: A nursing mother resumes duty after maternity leave. According to the seminar, she is entitled to—
options: three hours' time off every day for three months
two hours' time off every day for a maximum of six months from the date she resumed duty
