two hours' time off every week for six months
one hour's time off every day for twelve months
questions.explanation: The source specifies two hours' time off for nursing mothers every day, for a maximum period of six months from the date she resumed duty from maternity leave.

questions.question: A Ministry circulates a notice informing MDAs of a new government policy and amendments to existing policies. What is the best description of the instrument?
questions.explanation: The seminar describes a circular as a notice informing Chief Executives of Ministries and Extra-Ministerial Departments, Boards, Commissions and Government Parastatals about new policies or amendments to existing policies. Circulars guide and regulate government activities and services.

questions.question: A civil servant is reviewing his career records before a personnel-management process. He discovers letters concerning secondment/transfers, salary adjustments, records of indebtedness, tax records and sick leave. Which conclusion is MOST consistent with the seminar?
options: Only salary adjustment letters are career records; the others are purely financial documents.
Only transfer letters should be preserved because they affect deployment.
All the listed records are important career/personnel records and should be preserved and kept in custody as the officer progresses in the Service.
Tax and indebtedness records should be destroyed once the officer is confirmed.
questions.explanation: The seminar explicitly lists letters of secondment/transfers, salary adjustment letters, records of indebtedness, tax records and sick leave records among important personnel records. It then emphasizes that such records are important to an officer's career and should be preserved and kept in custody throughout the officer's service.

questions.question: Under the seminar material, recruitment of officers on Salary Grade Level 07 and above is carried out by the—
questions.explanation: The source states that recruitment of officers on GL 07 and above is done by the Civil Service Commission. It also states that recruitment of officers on GL 01–06 has been delegated to the respective Ministry or Department.

questions.question: A Ministry is recruiting an officer for a position on Salary Grade Level 05. Which arrangement is most consistent with the seminar?
options: The Civil Service Commission must personally conduct the recruitment because all recruitment belongs to the Commission.
The Ministry may conduct the recruitment because recruitment for GL 01–06 has been delegated to the respective Ministry or Department.
The Department of Establishments automatically conducts the recruitment.
The Senior Staff Management Committee conducts all recruitment irrespective of grade.
questions.explanation: The seminar states that although the Civil Service Commission handles recruitment at GL 07 and above, it has delegated recruitment of officers on GL 01–06 to the respective Ministry or Department.

questions.question: A recruiting authority wants to fill an existing vacancy but proposes appointing someone without reference to the applicable Scheme of Service. Which principle from the seminar has been overlooked?
options: The Scheme of Service should be strictly adhered to in making appointments to fill existing vacancies.
Appointment is entirely discretionary once a vacancy exists.
The APER must first be completed before any appointment can occur.
The Junior Staff Committee must approve every appointment.
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly states that the Scheme of Service should be strictly adhered to when appointing people to fill existing vacancies.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four types of appointment identified under PSR 020202 in the seminar?
options: Appointment on probation in a pensionable post
questions.explanation: The four types listed are probation in a pensionable post, non-pensionable/contract appointment, temporary appointment, and acting appointment. Permanent secondment is not one of the four types identified.

questions.question: An officer is appointed on a contract that varies between 12, 18 or 24 months. Which category of appointment does the seminar associate this with?
options: Appointment on probation in a pensionable post
questions.explanation: The source identifies appointment on a non-pensionable post (contract) as one of the four types, with the contract varying between 12, 18 or 24 months.

questions.question: An officer appointed on probation in a pensionable post completes the two-year probation period but fails to ensure that the appointment is confirmed. According to the seminar, what potential consequence is specifically mentioned?
questions.explanation: The seminar states that an officer on probation in a pensionable post should ensure confirmation on completion of two years, otherwise this may result in future stagnation.

questions.question: Which statement BEST distinguishes secondment from routine posting or deployment?
options: Secondment is simply the movement of an officer from one office to another within the same Ministry.
Secondment involves the temporary release of an officer to another government or approved body for a specified period.
Secondment is another name for promotion.
Secondment applies only to officers on Grade Level 01–06.
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly distinguishes secondment from routine posting/deployment and defines it as the temporary release of an officer to the service of another government or approved body for a specified period.

questions.question: An officer is temporarily released to another government body for a specified period. The arrangement was initiated because of public interest. Which statement is consistent with the seminar?
options: This may constitute secondment, which can be based on public interest or policy.
It cannot be secondment unless requested personally by the officer.
It is automatically an inter-ministerial transfer of service.
It is necessarily an acting appointment.
questions.explanation: The source states that secondment may be on the officer's request, on public interest or policy, depending on the circumstances.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a type of transfer of service in the seminar?
questions.explanation: The four types identified are Inter-Ministerial/Inter-Departmental, Inter-Service, Inter-Cadre and Inter-State Transfer of Service. There is no “Inter-Political-Party Transfer.”

questions.question: Promotion in the State Civil Service is described in the seminar primarily as—
options: a reward for hard work and a means of encouraging greater performance and productivity
an automatic consequence of completing APER
questions.explanation: The seminar describes promotion as a reward for hard work and a means of encouraging workers to perform better and enhance productivity.

questions.question: Which arrangement concerning promotion is correctly stated in the seminar?
options: Permanent Secretaries promote officers on GL 07–17 while the CSC promotes GL 01–06.
The CSC promotes officers on GL 07 and above, while Permanent Secretaries and Heads of Department have delegated authority to promote officers on GL 01–06.
The Junior Staff Committee promotes all officers below GL 07.
The Department of Establishments promotes every officer in the Service.
questions.explanation: The seminar states that promotion is essentially a function of the Civil Service Commission, but the Commission has delegated promotion of officers on GL 01–06 to Permanent Secretaries and Heads of Department, while the CSC promotes officers from GL 07 and above.

questions.question: Why are the Public Service Rules important in disciplinary administration according to the seminar?
options: They allow each manager to discipline officers according to personal preference.
They ensure continuity, predictability and uniform treatment in administrative action.
They eliminate the need for government circulars.
They apply only to junior officers.
questions.explanation: The seminar emphasizes that administrative action is bound by rules, which help ensure continuity, predictability and uniform treatment for all persons.

questions.question: A government circular amends a provision of the Public Service Rules. According to the seminar, what should the circular specifically state?
options: Only the name of the issuing officer
The aspect(s) or number(s) of the Public Service Rules being amended
The political party responsible for the amendment
The APER scores of affected officers
questions.explanation: The seminar states that government circulars and circular letters are issued to amend provisions of the PSRs and must specifically state the aspect(s)/number(s) of the rules amended.

questions.question: Which statement about the Civil Service Commission is MOST consistent with the seminar?
options: It is responsible only for recruitment and has no disciplinary function.
It is constitutionally responsible for appointing persons into the Civil Service, promotion and discipline of such persons.
It handles only officers on GL 01–06.
It is a department under the Personnel Directorate.
questions.explanation: The seminar describes the Civil Service Commission as constitutionally responsible for appointment, promotion and discipline of persons in the Civil Service.

questions.question: The Senior Staff Management Committee (SSMC) is considering a personnel matter involving an officer on Salary Grade Level 10. Which statement is most appropriate?
options: The SSMC handles matters for officers on GL 07–17 and makes recommendations to the Civil Service Commission for final determination.
The JSC handles the matter because all staff matters belong to the Junior Staff Committee.
The Permanent Secretary is automatically the final approving authority for every SSMC matter.
The Department of Establishments must first promote the officer before the SSMC can consider the matter.
questions.explanation: The source states that the SSMC handles matters concerning officers on GL 07–17 and makes recommendations to the Civil Service Commission for final determination.

questions.question: A personnel matter concerns an officer on Salary Grade Level 04. Which committee is responsible for handling matters within that grade range?
questions.explanation: The source states that the Junior Staff Committee (JSC) handles matters pertaining to officers on GL 01–06.

questions.question: A Junior Staff Committee makes a recommendation concerning an officer on GL 05. Who is identified in the seminar as the approving authority for JSC decisions and recommendations?
options: The Head of Civil Service personally
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically states that the Permanent Secretary is the approving authority for decisions and recommendations of the Junior Staff Committee.

questions.question: An officer disagrees with a decision of the Junior Staff Committee and wishes to challenge it. Which body is identified as receiving appeals arising from petitions against JSC decisions?
options: The Office of the Government Printer
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the SSMC receives appeals arising from petitions against decisions of the Junior Staff Committee.

questions.question: An officer decides to write directly to the Governor concerning a personnel matter without first passing through the relevant management committee. According to the seminar, this is—
options: the preferred method where the matter is urgent
permissible for officers on GL 07 and above
required where the officer disagrees with the Permanent Secretary
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly states that on no grounds should an officer write directly on personnel matters to the Head of Service or Governor without passing through the relevant management committees.

questions.question: A personnel manager believes an officer's petition has no merit and wants to dispose of it without committee consideration. Which response is MOST consistent with the principle of fair hearing in the seminar?
options: The manager may dispose of it because only meritorious petitions require consideration.
The manager should place the matter before the appropriate personnel-management committee regardless of the manager's personal view of its merit.
The manager should send it directly to the Governor.
The manager should first obtain the officer's APER before deciding whether the committee should see it.
questions.explanation: The fair-hearing principle is unusually explicit: all personnel matters, whether or not the personnel manager considers them meritorious, should be placed before the appropriate personnel-management committee for deliberation and appropriate recommendations to the final approving body.

questions.question: The primary purpose of staff training, according to the seminar, is to—
options: develop better skills, knowledge and attitude for effective and efficient job performance
enable officers to transfer between Ministries
replace the need for performance appraisal
questions.explanation: Training is intended to develop staff's skills, knowledge and attitude in ways that enhance effective and efficient job performance. Promotion may benefit from training, but it is not presented as the sole purpose.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the training provisions identified under Establishment Circular No. 1/2004?
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies in-service training, study leave with pay, study leave without pay and public service awards. Compulsory retirement training is not listed.

questions.question: An officer is approved for study leave with pay. Which statement is most accurate based on the seminar?
options: The officer receives no salary during the course.
The officer receives salary, and the course should normally not exceed four years.
The officer must retire after completing the course.
The officer is automatically transferred to the institution where the course is taken.
questions.explanation: Officers on study leave with pay continue to receive their salaries, and the duration of the course should not normally exceed four years, although exceptional approval may be granted for longer courses.

questions.question: Study leave without pay is intended primarily for officers who—
options: have already received study leave with pay and want another paid course
cannot benefit from in-service training, study leave with pay or a public service award and wish to acquire or sharpen skills
have been dismissed from the Service
questions.explanation: The material describes study leave without pay as being for officers who may not benefit from the other identified training avenues, enabling them to acquire knowledge and/or sharpen their skills.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes training, development and education as presented in the seminar?
options: Training concerns formal academic knowledge only, while education concerns workplace skills.

Training involves acquiring knowledge, skills and attitude for a particular assignment; development involves planned actions to improve skills and job experience; education involves acquiring formal background knowledge.
Development and education are simply different names for induction.
Training applies only to newly recruited officers.
questions.explanation: The source makes these distinctions explicitly: training is acquisition of knowledge, skills and attitude for an assignment; development is planned action to improve skills and job experience; education concerns formal background knowledge of a subject or course.

questions.question: A newly recruited officer is sent through an induction programme. Which of the following is MOST likely to be emphasized?
options: Loyalty to government and obedience to constituted authority
Personal business development during office hours
Avoidance of all interaction with the public
questions.explanation: Induction and orientation expose new staff to what is expected of government officers, including loyalty to government, punctuality, attendance, obedience to constituted authority, honesty and responsibility.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT identified as an expectation emphasized during induction and orientation?
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies the first three as induction/orientation expectations. Partisan political campaigning is not listed among them.

questions.question: A Director wants to prevent idleness and truancy and also make APER assessments more objective. Which measure from the seminar would BEST serve these purposes?
options: Allowing officers to choose their own scores
Giving every officer a clear Schedule of Duties
Reducing the number of officers in the Ministry
questions.explanation: A clear Schedule of Duties is intended to prevent idleness and truancy and ensure proper assessment. It also helps eliminate subjectivity and bias in performance assessment.

questions.question: An officer's APER is being completed, but the Reporting Officer cannot identify the specific duties against which the officer's performance should be judged. Which underlying personnel-management tool is most clearly missing?
questions.explanation: The seminar states that each officer should have a Schedule of Duties clearly spelling out what is expected, and annual performance reporting should be based on effective delivery against that schedule.

questions.question: Which statement about APER is correct according to the seminar?
options: It should be completed only when an officer becomes eligible for promotion.
It is completed annually for all officers at the end of each calendar year, whether or not they are mature or eligible for promotion.
It is required only for officers on GL 07 and above.
It is primarily a disciplinary document.
questions.explanation: The seminar states that APER should be administered on all officers at the end of each calendar year, regardless of whether an officer is mature or eligible for promotion.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT identified as a benefit or use of APER?
options: Assigning an officer to a new or specific job
questions.explanation: APER helps provide a record for judging suitability for promotion, identifying strengths and weaknesses/training needs, and assigning officers to new or specific jobs. Political affiliation is not a stated purpose.

questions.question: A Reporting Officer notices from an APER that an officer consistently performs poorly in a particular technical area. What is the most appropriate personnel-management response based on the seminar?
options: Ignore the weakness because APER is only for promotion.
Use the identified weakness to help determine the officer's training needs.
Transfer the officer without considering the nature of the weakness.
questions.explanation: APER provides an avenue for identifying an officer's strengths and weaknesses, which the Reporting Officer can use to determine training needs.

questions.question: Target setting is best described in the seminar as a process involving—
options: planned and goal-directed activities with steps and measurements for expected tasks within specified time and resources
questions.explanation: The seminar defines target setting as a process of improving performance through planned, goal-directed activities, providing steps and measurement for tasks to be implemented within a specified time and available resources.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as an element considered in target setting?
questions.explanation: The listed elements include quantity, quality, resources, time span, manner of performance and constraints/solutions to problems. Political preference is not among them.

questions.question: A supervisor sets a target requiring an officer to process 100 applications within five working days using specified available resources. Which two target-setting elements are most directly illustrated?
questions.explanation: “100 applications” establishes the quantity of output, while “five working days” establishes the time span of output. Both are expressly listed target-setting elements.

questions.question: A junior officer sends an official message directly to the top echelon while bypassing the immediate superior and established reporting route. Which communication principle has been disregarded?
options: The established line of command or communication
questions.explanation: The seminar advises officers to follow the established line of command or communication, moving from the officer to the immediate superior and then through the appropriate upper echelon.

questions.question: Which statement BEST describes effective communication according to the seminar?
options: Information should move only from management to junior staff.
Information should flow within the organization from the top down, from the bottom up and to the public.
Communication should be restricted to written correspondence.
Communication is complete once the sender sends the message.
questions.explanation: The stated goal is a flow of information from the top down, from the bottom to the top and to the public. The source also explains that communication involves a receiver interpreting, understanding and acting or reacting to the message.

questions.question: A Director sends a memorandum to a subordinate. The subordinate receives it but misunderstands its meaning and acts differently from what was intended. Which part of the communication process has most directly failed?
options: The transmission of a written document
The receiver's interpretation and understanding of the message
questions.explanation: The seminar describes communication as involving a sender initiating a message and a receiver who interprets, understands and acts or reacts to it. The problem described occurs at that receiver stage.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed among the elements of ethics in the seminar?
options: Political loyalty to a political party
questions.explanation: The seminar lists numerous ethical elements, including integrity, honesty, trustworthiness, accountability, punctuality, courtesy, probity, teamwork, cooperation, neutrality and professionalism. Political-party loyalty is not listed as an ethical element.

questions.question: An officer is highly competent but regularly ignores official procedures, treats members of the public discourteously and refuses to accept responsibility for mistakes. Which conclusion is MOST consistent with the seminar?
options: Competence alone is sufficient to establish ethical conduct.
The officer's conduct raises ethical concerns because professionalism, courtesy and accountability are among the identified elements of ethics.
The officer has no ethical issue unless financial misconduct is involved.
Ethics applies only to senior management officers.
questions.explanation: The seminar treats ethics broadly and identifies accountability, courtesy and professionalism, among other values, as elements of ethical conduct. Technical competence by itself does not satisfy the broader ethical standard.

questions.question: A Personnel Directorate notices that an existing personnel policy is creating a recurring administrative problem. It proposes a revision to the policy rather than merely advising officers on how to interpret the existing rule. Which personnel function is being performed?
questions.explanation: Policy initiation and formulation involves proposing and drafting new personnel policies or revisions to deal with recurring problems or prevent anticipated ones. Simply explaining an existing rule would fall under Advice.

questions.question: A Personnel Directorate is asked to explain how a recently issued circular should be applied by an MDA. No new policy is being proposed. Which function is most directly involved?
questions.explanation: The Advice function involves giving direction and coordination on rules, regulations, circulars and guidelines.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST illustrates the control function?
options: Advising an MDA on the meaning of a circular
Monitoring employee performance to ensure conformity with established personnel policies and practices
questions.explanation: Control involves monitoring employee performance to ensure conformity with established personnel policies, procedures and practices.

questions.question: A Personnel Directorate assists with recruitment, interviewing, employment, training, benefits, discipline and maintaining adequate employee service records up to retirement and beyond. Which personnel function encompasses these activities?
questions.explanation: The seminar places recruitment, interviewing, employment, training, benefits, discipline and maintenance of employee service records under the Service function of the Personnel Directorate.

questions.question: Which statement BEST explains why the Personnel Directorate is described as operating in an auxiliary advisory role?
options: It exists to replace all operating Directorates.
It exists to help line or operating Directorates perform their work more effectively and efficiently.
It has no responsibility for personnel matters.
It deals exclusively with financial administration.
questions.explanation: The source says staff Directorates exist to help line or operating Directorates do their work more effectively and efficiently, sustaining specialized talent, knowledge, coordination and standardization.

questions.question: An officer's APER identifies a weakness in a specialized area. The Reporting Officer recommends a course specifically designed to address that weakness. Which use of APER is being demonstrated?
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly states that the strengths and weaknesses identified through APER are used by the Reporting Officer to determine the officer's training needs.

questions.question: An officer is not yet eligible for promotion, but the Reporting Officer proposes that an APER should still be completed. Which statement supports the proposal?
options: APER is required only when promotion is imminent.
APER should be administered to all officers at the end of each calendar year, whether or not they are mature or eligible for promotion.
APER applies only to officers receiving training.
APER is optional for officers below GL 07.
questions.explanation: The source is explicit that APER is to be administered to all officers at the end of each calendar year, regardless of promotion maturity or eligibility.

questions.question: Which statement about APER is MOST accurate?
options: Its only purpose is to determine promotion.
It records work conduct and capabilities for promotion purposes but can also identify training needs and assist in job assignment.
It is primarily a disciplinary document.
It replaces the Schedule of Duties.
questions.explanation: The source identifies several uses of APER: creating a record from which promotion suitability may be judged, identifying strengths and weaknesses for training needs, and assigning officers to new or specific jobs to improve performance.

questions.question: A supervisor tells an officer: “You must process 80 applications within five working days using the available staff and equipment.” Which pair of target-setting elements is represented by “80 applications” and “five working days”, respectively?
questions.explanation: 80 applications establishes the quantity of output, while five working days establishes the time span of output. Both are expressly identified elements of target setting.

questions.question: An officer meets the required quantity and deadline but uses a method that is contrary to the expected procedure. Which target-setting element is most directly relevant?
questions.explanation: Manner of performance is separately identified as an element of target setting. Meeting the quantity and deadline does not by itself satisfy the required manner of performing the work.

questions.question: A supervisor sets a target but does not specify what resources may be used to achieve the required quantity of output. Which element has been overlooked?
options: Amount of resources to be utilized
questions.explanation: The source specifically identifies the amount of resources to be utilized for a given quantity of output as one of the six elements of target setting.

questions.question: Which combination contains only elements of target setting identified in the seminar?
options: Quantity, quality, resources and time span
questions.explanation: The seminar lists quantity, quality, resources, time span, manner of performance and constraints/solutions to problems as the elements of target setting.

questions.question: An officer applies for training. The application is first received and considered by the relevant body within the Ministry or pooling department before recommendations are forwarded for approval. Which body is identified in the seminar as receiving applications for training?
options: Office of the Head of Civil Service
questions.explanation: Applications for training of public servants are received by the respective Departmental Selection Board (DSB) of each Ministry or pooling department.

questions.question: An application for a study programme has been considered by the appropriate departmental body and recommendations have been made. According to the seminar, those recommendations are forwarded to—
options: the Civil Service Commission for automatic approval
the Department of Establishments for approval by the Head of Civil Service
the Governor for personal approval in every case
the Junior Staff Committee for final determination
questions.explanation: The seminar states that applications for study programmes are considered according to approved guidelines, after which the report and recommendations are forwarded to the Department of Establishments for approval by the Head of Civil Service.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT identified as a personnel-management responsibility of the Department of Establishments in the seminar?
options: Conducting all recruitment interviews for the State Civil Service
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies training, placement and grading, retirement, and serving as a clearing house through regulations on personnel-management matters at State level. It does not identify the Department of Establishments as responsible for conducting all Civil Service recruitment interviews.

questions.question: A personnel manager believes that an officer's petition is completely without merit and therefore refuses to place it before the appropriate management committee. Which principle is directly violated?
questions.explanation: The fair-hearing principle requires all personnel matters, whether the personnel manager considers them meritorious or not, to be placed before the appropriate personnel-management committee for deliberation and recommendation.

questions.question: Which statement BEST reflects the procedure required by the fair-hearing principle?
options: The personnel manager determines merit and only forwards meritorious matters.
Every personnel matter should be placed before the appropriate staff-management committee for consideration.
Every personnel matter must go directly to the Governor.
Only disciplinary matters require committee consideration.
questions.explanation: The source expressly says every matter must be placed before the appropriate staff management committee for consideration.

questions.question: A Ministry has a personnel matter involving an officer on GL 08. Which management body is identified as handling matters concerning officers within that grade range?
questions.explanation: The SSMC handles matters pertaining to officers on GL 07–17 and makes recommendations to the Civil Service Commission for final determination. Since GL 08 falls within that range, SSMC is the relevant body.

questions.question: An officer on GL 05 has a personnel matter before the appropriate management committee. Which statement is correct?
options: The SSMC handles the matter and the CSC approves it.
The JSC handles the matter, and the Permanent Secretary is the approving authority for its decisions and recommendations.
The Department of Establishments automatically makes the final decision.
The Governor must personally approve every JSC recommendation.
questions.explanation: The source states that the JSC handles officers on GL 01–06, while the Permanent Secretary is the approving authority for its decisions and recommendations.

questions.question: An officer disagrees with a JSC decision and wants to bypass the established process by writing directly to the Governor. What is the MOST appropriate response according to the seminar?
options: The officer may do so because the Governor is the ultimate authority.

The officer should first pass the matter through the relevant management committees; the seminar expressly prohibits direct writing to the Head of Service or Governor on personnel matters without doing so.
The officer should send the matter directly to the Department of Establishments.
The officer must first resign before appealing.
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly states that no officer should write directly on personnel matters to the Head of Service or Governor without passing through the relevant management committees. It also states that the SSMC receives appeals arising from petitions against JSC decisions.

questions.question: An officer on GL 04 is being considered for promotion by the JSC. The officer has spent two years on the grade, has an APER and appears on the seniority list. However, the prescribed examination required under the Scheme of Service has not been passed. What is the best conclusion based on the seminar?
options: The officer can be promoted because APER is sufficient.
The officer can be promoted because two years on the grade is the only mandatory requirement.
The officer cannot be considered because passing the prescribed examination is a prerequisite.
The officer can be promoted if the Permanent Secretary waives the examination.
questions.explanation: For the JSC promotion exercise, the seminar states that passing the prescribed examination in accordance with the Scheme of Service is a prerequisite for consideration.

questions.question: Which combination represents the correct weighting in the JSC promotion exercise described in the seminar?
questions.explanation: The seminar gives the weighting as Interview 70%, APER 20%, Seniority 10%, with an overall pass mark of 60%.

questions.question: An eligible junior officer scores 65% in the interview, 80% in APER and 90% for seniority. Using the weighting stated in the seminar, what is the officer's overall weighted score?
questions.explanation: Interview: 65 × 70% = 45.5 APER: 80 × 20% = 16 Seniority: 90 × 10% = 9 Total = 70.5%. Therefore the correct answer is C. This is exactly why we're doing QC. The calculation has to agree with the option. 🔧

questions.question: An officer scores 58% overall in the JSC promotion exercise but satisfies every other listed requirement. What does the seminar indicate?
options: The officer has passed because APER contributes 20%.
The officer has passed because the interview carries the greatest weight.
The officer has not attained the stated overall pass mark.
The officer automatically qualifies if the Permanent Secretary approves.
questions.explanation: The seminar specifies an overall pass mark of 60%. A score of 58% therefore falls below the stated threshold.

questions.question: A GL 05 officer satisfies the minimum two years on grade and passes the promotion assessment but has a pending disciplinary case. According to the seminar, what is required before promotion?
options: The disciplinary case must be cleared.
The officer must receive an additional APER.
The officer must be transferred to another Ministry.
The case is irrelevant once the examination is passed.
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically states that officers with pending disciplinary cases must be cleared before promotion.

questions.question: The Senior Staff Committee (SSC) is considering officers on which grade range according to the seminar?
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically states that the SSC handles GL 07–13 and recommends to the Civil Service Commission.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the SSC from the JSC under the seminar?
options: SSC handles GL 01–06, while JSC handles GL 07–13.
Both handle the same grades but have different chairpersons.
SSC handles GL 07–13, while JSC handles GL 01–06.
JSC handles GL 14–16, while SSC handles GL 01–06.
questions.explanation: The material assigns JSC to GL 01–06 and SSC to GL 07–13.

questions.question: An officer on GL 12 is being considered for promotion. Which requirement is specifically stated for the Senior Staff Committee level?
options: Minimum of two years on the post
Minimum of three years on the post
Minimum of four years on the post
questions.explanation: For the SSC level, the seminar states that a minimum of three years on post is required.

questions.question: Which body is identified as being chaired by the Permanent Secretary and composed of Directors in the relevant personnel-management structure?
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the Senior Staff Committee is composed of Directors and chaired by the Permanent Secretary.

questions.question: An officer is on GL 15 and has a disciplinary matter. According to the disciplinary allocation stated in the seminar, which body has responsibility?
questions.explanation: The seminar assigns disciplinary matters as follows: JSC — GL 01–06; SSC — GL 07–13; CSC — GL 14–16. Therefore GL 15 falls under the CSC.

questions.question: A disciplinary matter concerns a criminal offence committed by an officer. The MDA proposes treating it simply as administrative negligence. Which position is consistent with the seminar?
options: The matter should be treated as administrative negligence if no financial loss occurred.
Criminal matters must be charged to a Court of Competent Jurisdiction and should not be treated as administrative negligence.
Only the JSC can decide whether a crime occurred.
Criminal matters are automatically resolved through APER.
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly states that disciplinary cases on criminal matters must be charged to a Court of Competent Jurisdiction and no such matter should be treated as administrative negligence.

questions.question: Which situation BEST demonstrates the principle of fair hearing in staff discipline?
options: A manager dismisses an allegation after personally deciding it is weak.
A personnel manager considers a matter only if it appears meritorious.
A query is issued and the officer is given the opportunity to reply before the matter proceeds through the appropriate process.
An officer is punished first and allowed to explain afterwards.
questions.explanation: The material emphasizes fair hearing, including queries and replies as a basic fundamental right. It also requires personnel matters to be placed before the appropriate management committee for consideration.

questions.question: A Personnel Directorate is reviewing its records and discovers letters relating to an officer's secondment, salary adjustment, indebtedness and tax status. What does the seminar say about such records?
options: They are temporary administrative documents with no career significance.
They are important career records and should be preserved and kept in custody.
Only the salary adjustment letter needs to be preserved.
They should be destroyed once the officer is promoted.
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically identifies these records among important Public Service Career Records and states that they should be preserved and kept in custody as officers progress through the Service.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT identified in the material as a Public Service career record?
questions.explanation: The source specifically lists secondment/transfer letters, salary adjustment letters, records of indebtedness, tax records and sick-leave records among career records. A personal political manifesto is not listed.

questions.question: An officer argues that ethical conduct in government is simply another word for honesty. Which response BEST reflects the seminar?
options: Correct; honesty is the only element identified.
Correct, provided the officer is senior.
Incorrect; honesty is one element among several, including integrity, accountability, punctuality, courtesy, neutrality and professionalism.
Incorrect only because ethics means obedience to management.
questions.explanation: The seminar lists numerous elements of ethics, including integrity, honesty, trustworthiness, accountability, punctuality, courtesy, probity, teamwork, neutrality and professionalism.

questions.question: A junior officer needs to communicate an official matter to the upper echelon. Which route is most consistent with the seminar?
options: Junior officer → immediate superior → appropriate upper echelon
Junior officer → political party → Permanent Secretary
questions.explanation: The seminar advises officers to follow the established line of command or communication, with messages moving from the officer to the immediate superior and then to the upper echelon.

questions.question: Which of the following is a written communication method specifically identified in the seminar?
questions.explanation: The listed written communication methods include official correspondence, letters and endorsements; minuting in files and briefs; reports and memoranda; minutes of meetings; and file notes and enclosures.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes training from development?
options: Training is formal academic education, while development is disciplinary action.
Training is acquisition of knowledge, skills and attitude for a particular assignment, while development is planned action to improve skills and job experience in the current position.
Training is only for new recruits, while development is only for directors.
Training and development are defined identically in the seminar.
questions.explanation: The seminar explicitly defines training as acquisition of knowledge, skills and attitude to be applied at a particular assignment, while development is a planned set of actions to improve skills and job experience in an individual's current position.

questions.question: An officer wishes to undertake further formal academic study to obtain background knowledge in a subject rather than acquire skills specifically tied to one current assignment. Which concept most closely matches the seminar's definition?
questions.explanation: The seminar defines education as the process of acquiring formal background knowledge of a subject or course.

questions.question: A manager argues: “Because the Civil Service Commission has constitutional responsibility for appointment, promotion and discipline, no such power can ever be delegated.” Which statement from the seminar most directly challenges this conclusion?
options: The CSC has no constitutional personnel powers.
The CSC can delegate some of its duties, and Circular No. 1/2000 delegated specified appointment, promotion and disciplinary functions concerning GL 01–06 to MDAs.
Only the Governor can exercise personnel powers.
questions.explanation: The material describes the CSC as an independent body with constitutional personnel responsibilities but explicitly states that it can delegate some of its duties. It further identifies the delegation under Circular No. 1/2000 concerning officers on GL 01–06.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes personnel management according to the seminar?
options: The acquisition and utilization of human beings to accomplish organizational goals
The administration of government revenue and expenditure
The regulation of only senior civil servants
The supervision of government buildings and equipment
questions.explanation: The seminar defines Personnel Management as the arm of management concerned with the acquisition and utilization of human beings for accomplishing organizational goals, aims and objectives.

questions.question: Which of the following would fall outside the management activities listed in the seminar?
questions.explanation: The seminar associates management with activities such as recruitment, manpower planning, training, organization development, wages and salaries, incentives, motivation, communication, discipline and retirement. Land surveying and cadastral mapping is not identified as a personnel-management activity.

questions.question: A manager is planning how personnel will be acquired, organized and directed to achieve an MDA's objectives. Which set contains management functions expressly identified in the seminar?
options: Planning, Organising, Staffing, Directing and Controlling
questions.explanation: The seminar lists Planning, Organising, Staffing, Directing, Controlling, Coordinating, Reporting and Budgeting, represented by the acronym POSDCOKB.

questions.question: Which statement correctly reflects the constitutional role of the State Civil Service Commission as presented in the seminar?
options: It appoints and disciplines every employee in the entire State Public Service.
It appoints persons to offices in the State Civil Service and exercises disciplinary control over persons holding those offices.
It deals exclusively with training and retirement.
It only advises the Governor on recruitment.
questions.explanation: The seminar states that the constitutional provisions give the CSC power to appoint persons to offices in the State Civil Service and dismiss and exercise disciplinary control over persons holding such offices.

questions.question: A worker is employed by a State Public Service agency whose establishing arrangement gives appointment powers to its own Board rather than the Civil Service Commission. Which distinction in the seminar is relevant?
options: The CSC necessarily controls every employee in the State Public Service.
The State Civil Service consists of workers appointed by the CSC, while other Public Service employees may be appointed by various Commissions, Boards, Parastatals and Agencies.
No Public Service employee can be appointed by a Board.
The distinction depends entirely on the officer's salary grade.
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically distinguishes the State Civil Service from the wider State Public Service. It states that the CSC deals with employees appointed by it, while Public Service workers may be appointed by various Commissions, Boards, Parastatals and Agencies.

questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a source of information for personnel administration?
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies the 2022 Edition of the Akwa Ibom State Public Service Rules, among several sources of information, including the Constitution, Financial Instruction, Circulars, Treasury Circulars, Official Gazettes, Government White Papers, Personnel Records and Schemes of Service.

questions.question: Which combination contains only sources of information specifically identified in the seminar?
options: Public Service Rules, Circulars, Treasury Circulars and Personnel Records
Political manifestos, newspapers, social media and petitions
Staff gossip, advertisements, speeches and personal diaries
Electoral results, party constitutions, newspapers and social media
questions.explanation: The source expressly identifies Public Service Rules, Circulars, Treasury Circulars and Personnel Records, among others, as sources of information for personnel administration.

questions.question: A newly issued circular changes a provision of the Public Service Rules. What should the circular specifically identify according to the seminar?
options: The officer who will benefit from the amendment
The aspect(s) or number(s) of the Public Service Rules being amended
The annual APER score of affected officers
The political office responsible for the amendment
questions.explanation: The seminar states that circulars amending PSR provisions must specifically state the aspect(s)/number(s) of the rules amended.

questions.question: Which statement BEST describes the purpose of government circulars in the material?
options: They exist mainly to replace personnel records.
They guide and regulate government activities and services and may address matters such as appointments, promotion, leave, training and retirement.
They are issued only when an officer commits misconduct.
They apply exclusively to salary matters.
questions.explanation: The seminar describes circulars as notices informing government bodies about new policies or amendments to existing policies, with the purpose of guiding and regulating government activities and services.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the areas that circulars may regulate according to the seminar?
questions.explanation: The material lists areas including appointments, promotion, transfer, discipline, salaries, advancement, leave, housing, medical, taxation, training, retirement and protection of rights and privileges.

questions.question: An officer wants to preserve documents important to his career as he progresses through the Service. Which of the following is specifically identified as a career record?
questions.explanation: Letters of secondment/transfers are expressly listed among the Public Service career records that are important and should be preserved and kept in custody.

questions.question: Which of the following combinations contains only personnel career records identified in the seminar?
options: Salary adjustment letters, tax records and sick-leave records
Political party membership cards, tax records and newspapers
Personal photographs, salary slips and shopping receipts
Social-media records, tax records and election materials
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically identifies salary adjustment letters, tax records and sick-leave records, among the Public Service career records that should be preserved and kept in custody.

questions.question: Which statement about career records is MOST consistent with the seminar?
options: They are useful only during an officer's first year.
They are important throughout an officer's career and should be preserved and kept in custody as the officer progresses in the Service.
Only records relating to salary need to be preserved.
questions.explanation: The material emphasizes that the listed records are very important in an officer's career and should be preserved and kept in custody as the officer progresses through the Service.

questions.question: Which candidate satisfies the age requirement for a permanent/pensionable appointment stated in the seminar?
questions.explanation: The material states that a candidate for permanent/pensionable appointment should be not below 18 years and not above 50 years of age.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a requirement for permanent/pensionable appointment?
options: Possessing the required minimum qualification in the Scheme of Service
Being certified physically fit and mentally sound by a Government Medical Officer
Possessing a testimonial of conduct for past records
Having completed at least five years in private-sector employment
questions.explanation: The listed requirements include the required qualification, medical fitness, testimonial of conduct, certificate of origin, NYSC discharge/exemption certificate and other specified conditions. Five years of private-sector employment is not listed.

questions.question: A candidate satisfies the age and educational requirements but cannot provide the NYSC Discharge Certificate or Exemption Certificate required by the seminar. Which conclusion is most appropriate based strictly on the material?
options: The NYSC requirement is one of the stated requirements for permanent/pensionable appointment.
The requirement applies only to officers above GL 07.
The certificate is relevant only after promotion.
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly lists possession of an NYSC Discharge Certificate or Exemption Certificate among the requirements for permanent/pensionable appointment.

questions.question: Which candidate would fail one of the specific eligibility conditions stated in the seminar?
options: A candidate who is 30 years old and possesses the required qualification
A candidate who is medically certified fit and mentally sound
A candidate who was formerly dismissed from service
A candidate with an NYSC Exemption Certificate
questions.explanation: The seminar states that a candidate must not be an ex-convict or formerly dismissed from service.

questions.question: An officer is offered an appointment on probation in a pensionable post. Which statement is correct according to the seminar?
options: The probation period is one year and confirmation is automatic.
The probation period is two years, and the officer should ensure confirmation on completion to avoid possible future stagnation.
Probation applies only to temporary appointments.
Confirmation is unnecessary once the officer receives an APER.
questions.explanation: The seminar states that an officer appointed on probation in a pensionable post should ensure confirmation on completion of two years of probation, otherwise this may result in future stagnation.

questions.question: Which of the following is correctly matched with its appointment type?
options: Contract appointment — daily or monthly basis
Acting appointment — one of the four types specified under PSR 020202
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies acting appointment as one of the four types under PSR 020202. It distinguishes contract appointments, temporary appointments and probationary pensionable appointments separately.

questions.question: An officer is temporarily released to work for another government or approved body for a specified period. Which term does the seminar use for this arrangement?
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically defines secondment as the temporary release of an officer to the service of another Government or approved body for a specified period. It also emphasizes that secondment is different from routine posting or deployment.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST distinguishes personnel utilization from personnel motivation?
options: Utilization concerns salaries, while motivation concerns promotion.
Utilization concerns promotion, appraisal, training and development, while motivation includes salaries, fringe benefits and job satisfaction.
Utilization concerns discipline only, while motivation concerns recruitment only.
Both terms refer exclusively to staff protection.
questions.explanation: The material places promotion, appraisal, training and development under personnel utilization, while salaries, fringe benefits, job satisfaction, consultation and negotiation relate to personnel motivation.

questions.question: According to the seminar, the protection function of personnel management becomes meaningful when—
options: recruitment and promotion have been abolished
utilization and motivation functions have been properly looked after
every officer receives the same salary
questions.explanation: The material specifically states that the protection function is meaningful within the context in which the utilization and motivation functions have been looked after.

questions.question: A manager assigns an officer to a particular post and gives the officer specific responsibilities. Which aspect of personnel management does this BEST illustrate?
questions.explanation: The seminar describes deployment as the designation of officers, assignment of responsibilities and posting.

questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a basic tool of personnel management?
questions.explanation: The basic personnel-management tools identified include the Public Service Rules, Circulars, Schemes of Service, Annual Appropriation Laws and Financial Regulation.

questions.question: An officer argues that the Public Service Rules are concerned only with imposing obligations on public servants. Which statement from the material provides the best correction?
options: PSRs only regulate salaries and allowances.
PSRs guide staff in performing their duties and also secure their rights and privileges by stating the government's powers and responsibilities as employer.
PSRs apply only when disciplinary proceedings commence.
PSRs have no relationship with conditions of service.
questions.explanation: The material gives the PSRs a dual role: they provide guidance for staff in performing their duties and also secure public servants' rights and privileges by stating the powers and responsibilities of government as employer.

questions.question: A government agency discovers that an existing personnel rule has a gap that repeatedly causes administrative difficulties. Which purpose of a government circular most directly addresses this situation?
options: To replace the entire Public Service Rules
To fill a gap observed during implementation of a rule
To abolish the Scheme of Service
questions.explanation: The material states that government circulars may be issued to clarify a rule, fill a gap observed during implementation, or introduce a rule that was not there initially.

questions.question: Which statement BEST describes who may function as a personnel manager?
options: Only officers formally designated as Personnel Officers
Only Directors in the Directorate of Administration
Anyone involved in the day-to-day management of people and resources may perform personnel-management functions
Only members of the Civil Service Commission
questions.explanation: The seminar takes a broad view: anyone involved in the day-to-day management of people and resources performs personnel-management functions. It also notes that certain officers are specifically designated as Personnel Managers/Officers in the Civil Service.

questions.question: A Head of Section supervises several employees, deals with people seeking information and manages the resources under the section. Based on the seminar, the Head of Section—
options: cannot perform personnel functions because he is not a Director
is performing personnel-management functions and therefore acts as a personnel manager in that capacity
must first become a member of the Civil Service Commission
questions.explanation: The material expressly explains that managers such as Heads of Sections, Registries, Divisions, Departments or Directorates perform personnel functions because they manage people and resources.

questions.question: The Personnel Directorate is described as an auxiliary advisory structure. Its primary purpose is to—
options: help line or operating Directorates perform their work more effectively and efficiently
questions.explanation: The material explains that staff Directorates exist to help line or operating Directorates perform their work more effectively and efficiently, while sustaining specialized knowledge, coordination and standardization.

questions.question: Which personnel function involves giving direction and coordination on rules, regulations, circulars and guidelines?
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically defines Advice as giving direction and coordination concerning rules, regulations, circulars and guidelines.

questions.question: A Personnel Directorate proposes a new personnel policy because it anticipates a problem that has not yet become widespread. Which function is being performed?
questions.explanation: Policy initiation and formulation includes proposing and drafting new personnel policies or revisions to cover recurring problems or prevent anticipated problems.

questions.question: Which activity falls most directly under the Service function of the Personnel Directorate?
options: Monitoring compliance with existing personnel policies
Recruiting, interviewing, employment, training and maintenance of employee service records
Interpreting a circular for an MDA
questions.explanation: The Service function covers responsibilities including recruiting, interviewing, employment, training, benefits, discipline and maintaining adequate employee service records through retirement and beyond.

questions.question: A Personnel Directorate reviews whether employees are following established personnel policies, procedures and practices. This is primarily an example of—
questions.explanation: Control involves monitoring employee performance to ensure conformity with established personnel policies, procedures and practices.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes in-service training from study leave without pay as described in the material?
options: In-service training is sponsored through identified government training arrangements, while study leave without pay assists officers who may not benefit from the other specified training provisions.
Study leave without pay is exclusively for new recruits.
In-service training automatically results in promotion.
questions.explanation: The seminar states that in-service training is sponsored by the Department of Establishments in tertiary institutions, while study leave without pay is for officers who may not benefit from in-service training, study leave with pay or public service awards, to acquire knowledge or sharpen skills.

questions.question: Which statement about study leave with pay is correct according to the material?
options: Salary continues during the course, which should normally not exceed four years.
It is available only to officers who have already retired.
It is the same as study leave without pay.
questions.explanation: Officers on study leave with pay continue to receive their salaries, and the course should normally not exceed four years, although exceptional approval may be granted for longer courses.

questions.question: Which body is specifically identified as receiving applications for training from public servants?
questions.explanation: Applications for training are received by the relevant Departmental Selection Board (DSB) of each Ministry or pooling department.

questions.question: After study-programme applications are considered in accordance with the approved guidelines, where are the resulting reports and recommendations forwarded?
options: To the Civil Service Commission for automatic promotion
To the Department of Establishments for approval by the Head of Civil Service
To the Junior Staff Committee for disciplinary review
questions.explanation: The material states that the report and recommendations are forwarded to the Department of Establishments for approval by the Head of Civil Service.

questions.question: Which statement correctly matches the government personnel organ with its stated responsibility?
options: Office of the Head of Civil Service — coordinating all administrative functions of the State Public Service
Department of Establishments — conducting all political appointments
JSC — approving all matters concerning GL 07–17
SSMC — final approval of all JSC recommendations
questions.explanation: The material identifies the Office of the Head of Civil Service as coordinating all administrative functions of the State Public Service. The other options incorrectly assign responsibilities described elsewhere in the material.

questions.question: An officer has a personnel matter that he believes deserves urgent attention. He decides to bypass the relevant management committee and write directly to the Governor. According to the material, which statement is correct?
options: The officer may do so whenever the matter is urgent.
The officer may do so if the matter concerns promotion.
The officer should not do so; personnel matters should pass through the relevant management committees.
The officer must first publish the matter in a circular.
questions.explanation: The seminar expressly states that on no grounds should an officer write directly on personnel matters to the Head of Service or Governor without passing through the relevant management committees.

questions.question: Which statement brings together the central idea of personnel management in government most accurately?
options: Personnel management is primarily concerned with disciplining employees who violate government rules.
Personnel management is mainly the responsibility of the Civil Service Commission and therefore line managers have little role.

Personnel management concerns the effective and efficient utilization, motivation and protection of staff, supported by rules, procedures and personnel functions aimed at achieving organizational objectives.
Personnel management is essentially the administration of salaries and fringe benefits.
questions.explanation: This is the broadest and most accurate summary of the material. Personnel management in government encompasses utilization, motivation and protection of staff, while also dealing with policies, procedures, recruitment, deployment and the maintenance of an effective public organization. Its ultimate purpose is effective human-resource management in pursuit of organizational objectives.

questions.question: Which of the following is expressly identified as an element of ethics in the seminar?
questions.explanation: The seminar lists professionalism among the elements of ethics, alongside integrity, honesty, accountability, punctuality, neutrality and others.

questions.question: An officer demonstrates neutrality by—
options: Applying official responsibilities without partisan bias
questions.explanation: Neutrality is identified in the seminar as an element of ethical conduct in public service.

questions.question: Which of the following is specifically listed as a written method of communication in personnel administration?
questions.explanation: Minutes of meetings are expressly listed among the written communication methods in the seminar.

questions.question: The principal direction of communication recommended for a junior officer is through the—
questions.explanation: The seminar advises officers to follow the established line of command, communicating through the immediate superior and appropriate upper echelon.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT identified as an induction or orientation expectation?
questions.explanation: The seminar identifies punctuality, honesty and keeping the oath of secrecy as expectations, but does not identify personal political campaigning as an induction expectation.

questions.question: A Schedule of Duties is particularly useful because it helps to—
options: Define what an officer is expected to perform
questions.explanation: The seminar states that each officer should have a Schedule of Duties clearly spelling out what is expected, supporting proper assessment of performance.

questions.question: According to the seminar, APER is completed—
options: Annually at the end of each calendar year
Only when an officer requests promotion
Only for officers on GL 07 and above
questions.explanation: The seminar describes APER as an annual performance report completed at the end of each calendar year.

questions.question: A clear Schedule of Duties helps reduce subjectivity in APER primarily by—
options: Providing specific duties against which performance can be assessed
questions.explanation: The seminar explains that a clear Schedule of Duties supports objective assessment by establishing what the officer is expected to deliver.

questions.question: Which of the following is included among important Public Service career records?
questions.explanation: Sick-leave records are expressly identified among important Public Service career records.

questions.question: The seminar advises officers to preserve important career records because such records—
options: Remain important as officers progress through the Service
questions.explanation: The seminar states that career records should be preserved and kept in custody as officers progress through the Service.

questions.question: Which of the following is included in the seminar's list of ethical values?
questions.explanation: Probity is expressly included among the elements of ethics identified in the seminar.

questions.question: Effective communication in personnel administration should allow information to flow—
options: Top-down, bottom-up and to the public as appropriate
questions.explanation: The seminar describes effective communication as a flow of information within the organisation from the top down, from the bottom up and to the public.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes development as distinguished from training?
options: Planned action to improve skills and job experience in the current position
Formal background knowledge of a subject
Temporary release to another government body
questions.explanation: The seminar defines development as a planned set of actions intended to improve skills and job experience in an individual's current position.

questions.question: Which concept refers to acquiring formal background knowledge of a subject or course?
questions.explanation: The seminar distinguishes education as the process of acquiring formal background knowledge of a subject or course.

questions.question: A new officer is being introduced to government work and is taught punctuality, honesty and obedience to constituted authority. This is best described as—
questions.explanation: These are among the expectations specifically emphasized during induction and orientation programmes.

questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a purpose of a Schedule of Duties?
questions.explanation: The seminar states that a clear Schedule of Duties helps prevent idleness and truancy and supports proper performance assessment.

questions.question: A report, memorandum or address is treated in the seminar as a method of—
questions.explanation: Reports, memoranda and addresses are specifically listed among written communication methods in personnel administration.

questions.question: Which of the following most directly supports professional conduct in the public service?
questions.explanation: Integrity and accountability are both identified as elements of ethics in the seminar.

questions.question: When an officer communicates through the immediate superior before reaching a higher echelon, the officer is following the—
questions.explanation: The seminar specifically advises officers to follow the established line of command or communication.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a written communication method identified in the seminar?
questions.explanation: The seminar lists official correspondence, minutes, reports, memoranda, file notes and similar formal methods, not personal gossip.
